docs.text:
Bases: RuntimeError

Raised instead of a deprecation warning when a deprecation is configured as fatal.

Derives from :class:RuntimeError so an existing except Exception still catches it and no caller can mistake it for a :class:Warning subclass. The message is the same text the warning would have carried.

Examples:

>>> raise DeprecatedError("The `old_func` was deprecated since v1.0.")
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
deprecate._fatal.DeprecatedError: The `old_func` was deprecated since v1.0.
>>> issubclass(DeprecatedError, Warning)
False

docs.title: deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers(module, recursive=True, include_members=True, *, exclude=None, include_pep702=False)
docs.text:
Scan a module or package for deprecated wrappers and validate them.

This is a development/CI tool to scan a codebase for all wrappers created with :func:~deprecate.deprecated, :func:~deprecate.deprecated_class, :func:~deprecate.deprecated_instance, or :func:~deprecate.module.deprecated_module (module-level deprecation) and validate that each wrapper configuration is meaningful. Returns comprehensive information about each deprecated wrapper including validation results that help identify misconfigured wrappers.

A wrapper bound under several public names in one module is reported once, under the binding named like the wrapper (its __name__), so an unrelated alias never renames its row; when no binding carries that name (a private __name__, a deprecated class or instance proxy) the first public name in alphabetical order reports it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default module Union[Any, str]

A Python module or package to scan for deprecated wrappers. Can be: - Imported module object (e.g., import my_package; find_deprecation_wrappers(my_package)) - String module path (e.g., find_deprecation_wrappers("my_package.submodule"))

required recursive bool

If True (default), recursively scan submodules. If False, only scan the top-level module.

True include_members bool

If True, also scan deprecated methods and constructors defined on classes.

True exclude Optional[Sequence[str]]

Glob patterns (:func:fnmatch.fnmatchcase) over full dotted module names, e.g. ["my_package.tests", "*._legacy*"]. The walk itself never imports a matching submodule nor descends into a matching package (another module importing it still loads it), and no wrapper whose reported module matches is included (on a recursive=False package scan a re-export is attributed to the package itself, so it stays). None (default) excludes nothing.

None include_pep702 bool

If True, also report functions, classes, methods and property getters deprecated only with warnings.deprecated / typing_extensions.deprecated (PEP 702). Their rows classify api_type by shape like any other row (callable, class, class method, ...) and hold the decorator's message in pep702_message — a string, possibly empty, where every pyDeprecate row has None. Such objects carry no version schedule, so deprecated_info is empty and empty_deprecated_in is True; drop them (pep702_message is not None) before feeding the rows to schedule-based checks. A class member is reported only on the class that defines it, never again under a subclass, and the __new__ / __init_subclass__ hooks the decorator installs on a class are covered by the class row. A class bound under a second name (ShortName = LongName) lists its own PEP 702 members once, under the binding named like the class (LongName; the first name scanned when no binding is), while its pyDeprecate member rows still appear under each name. A module-level symbol whose __module__ lies in another top-level package (a deprecated helper imported from a dependency) is left out; one with an unknown __module__ is kept. A pyDeprecate wrapper with a PEP 702 decorator stacked on top is always a regular row. False (default) keeps every audit gate built on this scan unchanged.

False

Returns:

Type Description list[DeprecationWrapperInfo]

List of :class:~deprecate.audit.DeprecationWrapperInfo dataclasses, one per deprecated wrapper found: where

list[DeprecationWrapperInfo]

it is defined (module, function), its decorator metadata (deprecated_info) and every validation

list[DeprecationWrapperInfo]

field its attributes document.

Example

from deprecate import find_deprecation_wrappers from tests.collections.api_deprecated import core as my_package

results = find_deprecation_wrappers(my_package) print(len(results) > 0) # Should find deprecated wrappers True

Note
  • Requires that the module be importable
  • Recursive scans import every submodule of the package, executing their module-level code; packages with heavy import-time work (GPU init, network access) make the scan correspondingly expensive
  • Skips submodules that fail to import — any exception raised by module-level code, SystemExit included, is reported as a UserWarning (audit: skipped <module>: ...) and the scan continues
  • Inspects the __deprecation_config__ attribute set by the :func:~deprecate.deprecated decorator
  • Skips private/magic attributes and imports from other modules
  • Uses static member inspection to avoid scan-time side effects from dynamic attribute access

docs.title: Also works with string module paths
docs.text: results = find_deprecation_wrappers("tests.collections.api_deprecated.core") print(len(results) > 0) True

docs.title: Filter to find only problematic wrappers
docs.text: problematic = [r for r in results if r.invalid_args or r.no_effect] print(len(results) > 0) # May or may not have problematic ones True

docs.title: deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers_static(path, recursive=True, include_members=True, *, exclude=None)
docs.text:
Read deprecated wrappers from Python source without importing or executing the scanned package.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path Union[str, PathLike[str]]

Package directory, module file, plain directory, or top-level module name located without importing it. Dotted module names are refused because locating them would import their parents.

required recursive bool

Read package submodules recursively; plain directories include only top-level Python files.

True include_members bool

Include deprecated class members.

True exclude Optional[Sequence[str]]

Glob patterns over dotted module names, as in :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers; None excludes nothing.

None

Returns:

Type Description StaticScanResult

Source-derived rows, ordered gaps, and the version resolved without imports. Always inspect gaps before

StaticScanResult

treating an empty wrappers tuple as clean. Targets are stand-ins, not executable replacements.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the location has no Python source or requires importing parent packages to locate it.

Examples:

>>> from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
>>> with TemporaryDirectory() as root:
...     package = Path(root, "sample")
...     package.mkdir()
...     _ = (package / "__init__.py").write_text(
...         "from deprecate import deprecated\n"
...         "@deprecated(deprecated_in='1.0', remove_in='2.0')\ndef old(): pass\n"
...     )
...     result = find_deprecation_wrappers_static(package)
...     [row.function for row in result.wrappers], result.gaps
(['old'], ())

docs.title: deprecate.audit.StaticScanResult dataclass
docs.text:
Keep the rows, gaps, and version of an import-free source scan together.

Rows are approximations read from source and carry stand-in targets that raise TypeError when called. Callers must read gaps: empty wrappers with non-empty gaps is not a clean result.

Attributes:

Name Type Description wrappers tuple[DeprecationWrapperInfo, ...]

Static wrapper rows after module exclusions.

gaps tuple[str, ...]

Structural gaps in encounter order, then distinct unresolved-setting details for each row.

version Optional[str]

Package version resolved without importing, or None when unavailable.

Examples:

>>> from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
>>> with TemporaryDirectory() as root:
...     _ = Path(root, "module.py").write_text("value = 1\n")
...     scan = find_deprecation_wrappers_static(root)
...     scan.wrappers, scan.gaps
((), ())

docs.title: deprecate.audit.validate_deprecation_wrapper(func)
docs.text:
Validate a deprecated callable or module wrapper and return structured metadata.

This is a development tool to check if deprecated wrappers are configured correctly and will have the intended effect. It examines the __deprecation_config__ attribute set by the :func:~deprecate.deprecated decorator and identifies configurations that would result in zero impact:

  • args_mapping keys that don't exist in the function's signature
  • Empty or None args_mapping (no argument remapping)
  • Identity mappings where key equals value (e.g., {'arg': 'arg'})
  • Target pointing to the same function (self-reference)
  • target=None with no args_mapping (just warns, no forwarding)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default func Union[Callable, ModuleType]

The deprecated wrapper to validate. Accepts either a callable decorated with @deprecated or a module object passed through :func:deprecated_module. Must have a __deprecation_config__ attribute.

required

Returns:

Type Description DeprecationWrapperInfo
  • function: Name of the wrapper being validated
  • deprecated_info: The typed :class:~deprecate._types.DeprecationConfig metadata from __deprecation_config__
  • invalid_args: List of args_mapping keys not in wrapper signature
  • empty_args_mapping: True if args_mapping is None or empty
  • identity_args_mapping: List of args where key equals value (no effect)
  • self_reference: True if target is the same as the wrapper
  • no_effect: True if wrapper has zero impact (all checks combined)
  • empty_deprecated_in: True when deprecated_in is absent or empty

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the wrapper has missing or invalid __deprecation_config__ metadata (expected :class:~deprecate._types.DeprecationConfig).

Example

from deprecate import TargetMode, deprecated, validate_deprecation_wrapper def new_implementation(value: int) -> int: ... return value * 2

@deprecated(target=new_implementation, deprecated_in="1.0", args_mapping={"old_val": "value"}) ... def old_func(old_val: int) -> int: ... pass

Note

Use this function during development or in CI to ensure deprecation decorators are configured meaningfully. Invalid configurations won't cause runtime errors but will silently have no effect.

docs.title: Valid mapping to different function - has effect
docs.text:
result = validate_deprecation_wrapper(old_func) result.no_effect False result.invalid_args []

@deprecated(target=TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP, deprecated_in="1.0", args_mapping={"arg": "arg"}) ... def identity_func(arg: int) -> int: ... return arg

docs.title: Identity mapping with self-deprecation - no effect
docs.text: result = validate_deprecation_wrapper(identity_func) result.identity_args_mapping ['arg'] result.no_effect True

docs.title: deprecate.audit.validate_deprecation_expiry(module, current_version=None, recursive=True, include_members=True, *, exclude=None)
docs.text:
Check all deprecated callables in a module/package for expired removal deadlines.

This enforcement tool scans an entire module or package for deprecated functions and checks if any have passed their scheduled removal version. It's designed for CI/CD pipelines to automatically detect and report zombie code across a codebase.

For module inputs, the function uses :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers to discover deprecated wrappers; a static result supplies its already-scanned rows. Wrappers that have reached or passed their removal deadline are collected and reported.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default module Union[Any, str, StaticScanResult]

A Python module or package to scan. Can be: - Imported module object (e.g., import my_package; validate_deprecation_expiry(my_package, "2.0")) - String module path (e.g., validate_deprecation_expiry("my_package.submodule", "2.0")) - :class:~deprecate.audit.StaticScanResult, checked without imports or another scan; only rows with resolved expiry settings are checked. Inspect its gaps for incomplete coverage.

required current_version Optional[str]

The current version of your package to compare against removal deadlines (e.g., "2.0.0"). If None, auto-detects the version of the top-level package of the module path (e.g. "mypackage" for "mypackage.submodule") the way the CLI does: installed metadata under the import name, then under the distribution that ships it, then the package's string __version__. For a static result, uses its version instead, raising ImportError if it is unavailable.

None recursive bool

If True (default), recursively scan submodules. If False, only scan the top-level module.

True include_members bool

If True (default), also scan deprecated class members (methods, constructors, classmethods, staticmethods, properties) — matching the discovery default of :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers, so the enforcement gate sees everything discovery and reporting see.

True exclude Optional[Sequence[str]]

Glob patterns over full dotted module names to leave out of the scan, as in :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers (e.g. ["my_package.tests"]); None excludes nothing.

None

Returns:

Type Description list[str]

List of error messages for callables that have expired (past their removal deadline).

list[str]

Empty list if all deprecated callables are still within their deprecation period.

Raises:

Type Description ImportError

If packaging is not installed, or if current_version is None and no version can be resolved for the package. A string module path that cannot be imported raises ModuleNotFoundError (an ImportError subclass).

ValueError

If current_version is not a valid PEP 440 version, if module is an empty string, or if current_version is None and module is an object without a __name__. Also raised for a static result with recursive=False or include_members=False: scan options are already fixed.

Exception

Any other error raised by the import-time code of a string module path (for example a RuntimeError) propagates unchanged, with or without current_version. With current_version=None the import runs before the version lookup, so this error is reported instead of a missing version.

Example

Note

  • Skips callables without a remove_in field (warnings only, no removal deadline)
  • Skips callables that cannot be imported or accessed
  • Emits a UserWarning (rather than silently skipping) for callables with an unparsable remove_in
  • Uses semantic versioning comparison (e.g., "1.2.3" vs "2.0.0")
  • Intended for automated checks in CI/CD pipelines
  • Can be integrated into test suites or pre-commit hooks

docs.title: Check a specific module with version before any deadlines
docs.text: from deprecate import validate_deprecation_expiry expired = validate_deprecation_expiry("tests.collections.api_deprecated.core", "0.1", recursive=False) len(expired) 0

docs.title: Check with version past some removal deadlines
docs.text: expired = validate_deprecation_expiry("tests.collections.api_deprecated.core", "0.5", recursive=False) print(len(expired)) # Some functions and class members have remove_in <= "0.5" 31

docs.title: deprecate.audit.validate_deprecation_policy(module, recursive=True, include_members=True, *, min_grace=_DEFAULT_MIN_GRACE, message_required=_DEFAULT_MESSAGE_REQUIRED, exclude=None)
docs.text:
Check every deprecated wrapper in a module/package against deprecation-governance rules.

Where :func:~deprecate.audit.validate_deprecation_expiry answers "was this removed on time?", this gate answers "was this scheduled responsibly in the first place?" — catching a removal deadline that leaves callers too short a grace window or lands off a release boundary, and a warning that never names a replacement, all at review time instead of in a downstream issue.

Two rules are checked, each independently switchable (None/False disables):

  • min_grace — remove_in must be one clean version bump beyond deprecated_in, at least this far (default "0.3", three minors).
  • message_required — every wrapper must name a replacement (target, mapping, or custom template).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default module Union[Any, str, StaticScanResult]

A Python module or package to scan — an imported module object or a string module path. Also accepts a :class:~deprecate.audit.StaticScanResult without imports or another scan; each rule checks only rows whose required settings resolved. Inspect its gaps for incomplete coverage.

required recursive bool

If True (default), recursively scan submodules.

True include_members bool

If True (default), also scan deprecated class members, matching the discovery default of :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers.

True min_grace Optional[GraceWindowSpec]

Minimum grace window, either a version-shaped delta with two or three components — "1.0" (one major), "0.3" (three minors), "0.0.2" (two patches); a float such as 0.3 works too — or a one-key table naming the unit: {"major": 1}, {"minor": 3}, {"patch": 2}; every spelling is converted to a :class:~deprecate.audit.GraceWindow up front, which can also be passed directly. None skips the rule; a bare "1" is rejected as ambiguous. The removal has to be a clean bump of one component with everything below it reset (1.2 → 1.5 or 2.0, never 2.3); a coarser bump always satisfies the window regardless of the count (1.2 → 2.0 clears "0.3"), a finer one never does. The count restricts distance only within its own component.

_DEFAULT_MIN_GRACE message_required bool

Require migration guidance on every wrapper.

_DEFAULT_MESSAGE_REQUIRED exclude Optional[Sequence[str]]

Glob patterns over full dotted module names to leave out of the scan, as in :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers (e.g. ["my_package.tests"]); None excludes nothing.

None

Returns:

Type Description list[str]

List of violation messages, each prefixed with its :class:~deprecate.audit.PolicyRule slug.

list[str]

Empty list when every wrapper satisfies the enabled rules.

Raises:

Type Description ImportError

If min_grace is enabled, a wrapper carries both version fields, and the packaging library is not installed (pip install pyDeprecate[audit]). A policy reduced to message_required alone parses no version and runs without it.

ValueError

If min_grace is not a valid specification, or a static result is given with recursive=False or include_members=False because its scan options are already fixed.

Examples:

>>> from deprecate import validate_deprecation_policy
>>> violations = validate_deprecation_policy("tests.collections.policy", recursive=False)
>>> [v for v in violations if "no_grace_window" in v]
['[min-grace] Callable `tests.collections.policy.no_grace_window` is deprecated in `2.0` and ...']

>>> # Rules are opt-out: keep the guidance rule, drop the grace window
>>> violations = validate_deprecation_policy("tests.collections.policy", recursive=False, min_grace=None)
>>> any("min-grace" in v for v in violations)
False

Note

  • A 0.x project needs no special setting: a bump to 1.0 is a major step and clears any window, while removals within the 0.x line are measured in minors as usual.
  • Wrappers missing deprecated_in or remove_in are not violations here — the grace-window rule simply skips them (a deprecation without a scheduled removal is a valid, common choice).
  • An unparsable version string emits a UserWarning per skip rather than aborting the scan; a grace window whose two versions sit in different PEP 440 epochs is skipped and warned about the same way, since release numbers are not comparable across an epoch change.
  • Intended for the same CI slot as the expiry gate; the CLI exposes it as pydeprecate policy.

docs.title: deprecate.audit.validate_deprecation_chains(module, recursive=True, include_members=True, *, exclude=None)
docs.text:
Validate that deprecated functions don't form chains with other deprecated code.

This is a developer utility that scans a module or package for deprecated functions that form chains in two ways:

  1. TARGET chains: The target argument points to another deprecated callable instead of the final non-deprecated implementation.
  2. STACKED chains: Multiple @deprecated(target=TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP, ...) decorators are stacked on the same function with argument mappings that should be collapsed, or a callable target is itself a self-deprecation (target=TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP) requiring mapping composition.

Both types are wasteful: wrappers should point directly to the final (non-deprecated) implementation with composed argument mappings.

Detection is based purely on decorator metadata (__deprecation_config__ attributes) — no source-code or AST inspection is performed.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default module Union[Any, str]

A Python module or package to scan for deprecation chains. Can be: - Imported module object (e.g., import my_package; validate_deprecation_chains(my_package)) - String module path (e.g., validate_deprecation_chains("my_package.submodule"))

required recursive bool

If True (default), recursively scan submodules. If False, only scan the top-level module.

True include_members bool

If True (default), also scan deprecated class members (methods, constructors, descriptors), matching :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers. Pass False to check module-level wrappers only.

True exclude Optional[Sequence[str]]

Glob patterns over full dotted module names to leave out of the scan, as in :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers (e.g. ["my_package.tests"]); None excludes nothing.

None

Returns:

Type Description list[DeprecationWrapperInfo]

List of :class:~deprecate.audit.DeprecationWrapperInfo where chain_type is not None, i.e. every

list[DeprecationWrapperInfo]

deprecated wrapper that forms a chain (ChainType.TARGET or ChainType.STACKED).

Example

from deprecate import validate_deprecation_chains import tests.collections.chains as test_module

issues = validate_deprecation_chains(test_module, recursive=False) len(issues) > 0 # Should find chains True

Note
  • Only flags callees using the :func:~deprecate.deprecated decorator
  • Uses :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers and inspects chain_type to detect chains

docs.title: deprecate.audit.validate_mapping_compatibility(module, recursive=True, include_members=True, *, exclude=None)
docs.text:
Return wrappers whose args_mapping remaps deprecated names to POSITIONAL_ONLY constructor params.

A non-empty args_mapping_positional_only on the returned DeprecationWrapperInfo identifies mappings whose values the proxy forwards positionally to the constructor. Use this validator for advisory visibility into :func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_class mappings that require positional forwarding.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default module Union[Any, str]

A Python module or package to scan. Accepts an imported module object or a dotted module path string.

required recursive bool

When True (default) recursively scan submodules.

True include_members bool

When True (default) also scan class members, so a deprecated_class proxy bound as a class attribute is checked too, matching :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers. Pass False to check module-level wrappers only.

True exclude Optional[Sequence[str]]

Glob patterns over full dotted module names to leave out of the scan, as in :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers (e.g. ["my_package.tests"]); None excludes nothing.

None

Returns:

Type Description list[DeprecationWrapperInfo]

List of DeprecationWrapperInfo instances whose args_mapping_positional_only field is

list[DeprecationWrapperInfo]

non-empty. Returns an empty list when no such mappings are found.

Examples:

>>> from deprecate import validate_mapping_compatibility
>>> import tests.collections.api_deprecated.core as col
>>> results = validate_mapping_compatibility(col, recursive=False)
>>> len(results) > 0  # DepPositionalOnly remaps to a POSITIONAL_ONLY param
True
>>> results[0].function
'DepPositionalOnly'

docs.title: deprecate.audit.generate_deprecation_table(module, current_version=None, recursive=True, style=TableStyle.COMPACT, include_members=True, *, exclude=None)
docs.text:
Generate a markdown table summarizing deprecated wrappers.

The table is derived from __deprecation_config__ metadata and includes both top-level wrappers and deprecated class members (methods/constructors).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default module Union[Any, str, StaticScanResult]

Imported module/package object or string module path to scan. Also accepts a :class:~deprecate.audit.StaticScanResult without imports or another scan. Its source rows are rendered as-is with stand-in target names; inspect gaps for unresolved settings and incomplete coverage.

required current_version Optional[str]

Optional current package version for lifecycle status evaluation in compact style. If None, the version is auto-detected like validate_deprecation_expiry does; status falls back to "⚪ Status Unknown" when it stays unresolved or packaging is not installed. For a static result, defaults to its version without any further lookup.

None recursive bool

If True (default), include submodules in the scan.

True style Union[TableStyle, str]

Table format — "compact" or "matrix". - "compact": Original API | API Type | New API | Deprecated | Remove | Current Status - "matrix": Original API | API Type | New API | <all versions...>, with markers D (deprecated) and R (remove) in version columns; D/R marks a release that is both deprecated and removed. There is one column per release: spellings such as 1.0, v1.0 and 1.0.0 merge into one column when packaging is installed, and without it only the v prefix is ignored.

COMPACT include_members bool

If True (default), include deprecated class members (methods, constructors).

True exclude Optional[Sequence[str]]

Glob patterns over full dotted module names to leave out of the scan, as in :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers (e.g. ["my_package.tests"]); None excludes nothing.

None

Returns:

Type Description str

Markdown string containing a formatted table. When a version is

str

resolvable (either from current_version or auto-detected), the

str

first line is an HTML comment

str

followed by the header row and alignment row. When no version can be

str

resolved, the first line is the header row directly.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If style is not "compact" or "matrix", or if current_version is supplied explicitly but is not a valid PEP 440 version string and packaging is installed. Also raised for a static result with recursive=False or include_members=False because its scan options are already fixed.

Example

from tests.collections.api_deprecated import core as pkg report = generate_deprecation_table(pkg, recursive=False) report.splitlines()[0] '| Original API | API Type | New API | Deprecated | Remove | Current Status |'

docs.title: deprecate.audit.DeprecationWrapperInfo dataclass
docs.text:
Information about a deprecated wrapper and its validation results.

This dataclass represents a deprecated wrapper (a :func:~deprecate.deprecated-decorated function or a :func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_class/:func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_instance proxy), containing both identification info and validation results from :func:~deprecate.audit.validate_deprecation_wrapper or :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers.

Attributes:

Name Type Description module str

Module name where the wrapper is defined (empty for direct validation).

function str

Wrapper name.

deprecated_info DeprecationConfig

The __deprecation_config__ attribute from the decorator, as a :class:~deprecate._types.DeprecationConfig.

invalid_args list[str]

List of args_mapping keys that don't exist in the wrapper's signature.

empty_args_mapping bool

True if args_mapping is None or empty (no argument remapping).

identity_args_mapping list[str]

List of args where key equals value (e.g., {'arg': 'arg'}).

self_reference bool

True if target points to the same wrapper.

no_effect bool

True if wrapper has zero impact (combines all checks).

all_identity bool

True when every configured mapping is an identity mapping (key == value, non-empty).

chain_type Optional[ChainType]

The kind of deprecation chain detected, or None if no chain. See :class:~deprecate.audit.ChainType for values (:attr:~deprecate.audit.ChainType.TARGET or :attr:~deprecate.audit.ChainType.STACKED).

misconfigured_target bool

True when the wrapper has an invalid target configuration: target=False, :attr:~deprecate._types.TargetMode.NOTIFY with args_mapping, args_extra or attrs_mapping, :attr:~deprecate._types.TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP with empty args_mapping, or args_mapping/args_extra on a served object that is not callable (:attr:~deprecate._types.DeprecationConfig.call_options_inert).

empty_deprecated_in bool

True when deprecated_in is empty. Missing remove_in alone is a valid use case (many libraries deprecate without a scheduled removal date), so only the absence of deprecated_in is treated as a misconfiguration signal. CI pipelines can filter on this field to surface wrappers that lack the introductory version metadata without crashing callers.

api_type str

Inferred deprecated API type for report generation. Possible values: callable, args, class, dataclass, dataclass attributes, data, module, class constructor, class constructor args, class method, class method args, classmethod, classmethod args, staticmethod, staticmethod args. A row for an object deprecated only with warnings.deprecated/typing_extensions.deprecated gets the same shape classification; pep702_message marks it.

args_mapping_auto_expanded list[str]

args_mapping keys that were automatically copied from attrs_mapping by the dataclass dual-surface expansion at decoration time. Empty list when no auto-expansion occurred. Read from :attr:~deprecate._types.DeprecationConfig.args_mapping_auto_expanded.

args_mapping_positional_only list[str]

args_mapping old-key names whose remapped target is a POSITIONAL_ONLY constructor parameter. A non-empty list identifies mappings whose values the proxy forwards positionally to the constructor. Use :func:~deprecate.audit.validate_mapping_compatibility to filter wrappers by this field. Read from :attr:~deprecate._types.DeprecationConfig.args_mapping_positional_only.

inner_order_property bool

True when the wrapper is a plain :class:property whose fget carries @deprecated metadata — the inner order @property @deprecated (@deprecated closer to def). In this order only fget warns; any setter or deleter added afterwards is built from the plain :class:property base and is silently unprotected. The flag fires for every inner-order property, including the getter-only shape, because the canonical order is the outer @deprecated(...) @property (which produces a :class:~deprecate._properties._DeprecatedProperty that re-wraps every rebound accessor). CI pipelines can filter on this field to reject the silent write/delete gap. False for outer-order properties, non-property wrappers, and proxies.

pep702_message Optional[str]

None for every pyDeprecate wrapper. On a row that :func:~deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers reports with include_pep702=True for an object deprecated only with warnings.deprecated/typing_extensions.deprecated, the message that decorator recorded on __deprecated__ — a string, possibly empty. It is the only metadata such an object carries, so deprecated_info holds no versions or target and empty_deprecated_in is True.

source_file Optional[str]

Absolute path of the file that defines the deprecated object, or None when it has none: a :func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_instance data object, a class built at runtime (a functional Enum or a type() call), or a function compiled from a string. A class built by exec in a namespace named after a real module may be attributed to that module's file (Python 3.13+). For a deprecated module it is the module's file.

source_line Optional[int]

First line of the definition — the line of its first decorator — or None with no source_file and for a deprecated module. Neither field takes part in equality or repr.

Example

info = DeprecationWrapperInfo( ... module="my_package.module", ... function="old_function", ... deprecated_info=DeprecationConfig(deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0"), ... invalid_args=["nonexistent"], ... no_effect=True, ... ) info.function 'old_function' info.invalid_args ['nonexistent']

docs.title: deprecate.audit.ChainType
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

Type of deprecation chain detected by :func:~deprecate.audit.validate_deprecation_chains.

Attributes:

Name Type Description TARGET

The target argument is itself deprecated — a callable decorated with :func:~deprecate.deprecated or a deprecated proxy, including a :func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_instance data object (a forwarding chain). Fix by pointing directly to the final non-deprecated target.

STACKED

Arg mappings chain and must be composed/collapsed. Two sub-cases: (a) Callable target is itself @deprecated(True, args_mapping=...) — the caller's mapping feeds into the target's self-renaming, so both hops must be collapsed into one. (b) Multiple @deprecated(True, args_mapping=...) decorators are stacked on the same function and should be merged into a single decorator. Also used when attrs_mapping values point at another deprecated attribute alias.

docs.title: deprecate.audit.PolicyRule
docs.text:
Bases: str, Enum

Governance rule checked by :func:~deprecate.audit.validate_deprecation_policy.

Each member's value is the slug that prefixes the rule's violation messages, so a CI log can be grouped or filtered by rule. Every rule is switched by its own keyword argument, mirrored by a pydeprecate policy flag of the same name.

Attributes:

Name Type Description MIN_GRACE

remove_in must be one clean bump of a single version component beyond deprecated_in, at least min_grace steps of it -- a version-shaped delta: "0.3" three minors (default), "1.0" one major, "0.0.2" two patches; None disables. A coarser bump clears a finer window (1.2 -> 2.0 satisfies "0.3"), a mixed bump never passes (1.2 -> 2.3 is neither a major nor a minor step), and a remove_in at or before deprecated_in always fails. Versions spanning a PEP 440 epoch, or that do not parse, are skipped with a :class:UserWarning.

MESSAGE_REQUIRED

the wrapper must name what to migrate to -- a callable or module target, a non-empty args_mapping/attrs_mapping, or a non-empty custom message_template; message_required=False disables. An explicit :attr:~deprecate.TargetMode.NOTIFY counts only the template; a data replacement passed as deprecated_instance(target=...) counts only with an attrs_mapping or the template; a deprecated module counts its replacement module, its attrs_mapping, or a template other than the built-in notice :func:~deprecate.module.deprecated_module renders when given none. The one rule that runs without packaging.

Examples:

>>> PolicyRule.MIN_GRACE.value
'min-grace'

docs.title: deprecate.audit.GraceWindow dataclass
docs.text:
Strict form of a min_grace window: count steps of exactly one version component unit.

This is what every user-facing spelling is converted into before a policy scan starts, so the single-unit rule is structural rather than something each consumer re-checks: an instance cannot name two units, and construction rejects a negative or non-integer count. Build one directly, or from any accepted spelling with :meth:parse — a dotted delta ("0.3"), the float a TOML file may hand over, or a one-key table.

Attributes:

Name Type Description count int

Minimum number of bumps required; 0 disables the distance check while still requiring a clean bump of unit or coarser.

unit VersionBump

Version component the bumps are counted in.

Examples:

>>> GraceWindow(3, VersionBump.MINOR)
GraceWindow(count=3, unit=<VersionBump.MINOR: 'minor'>)
>>> GraceWindow(-1, VersionBump.MINOR)
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: Invalid `min_grace` specification `GraceWindow(count=-1, ...)`; ...

docs.title: __post_init__()
docs.text: Reject a count or unit no accepted spelling could have produced.

docs.title: describe()
docs.text:
Render the window as prose, e.g. "1 minor release" or "2 major releases".

Examples:

>>> GraceWindow(1, VersionBump.MINOR).describe()
'1 minor release'
>>> GraceWindow(0, VersionBump.PATCH).describe()
'0 patch releases'

docs.title: parse(min_grace) classmethod
docs.text:
Convert any accepted min_grace spelling into a :class:GraceWindow.

Two spellings, plus an instance passed through unchanged. The dotted delta is shaped like a version with two or three components and a single non-zero one — its position is the unit, the number the count: "1.0" one major, "0.3" three minors, "0.0.2" two patches. A bare "1" is rejected as ambiguous (write "1.0"), and so is "1.2" — two units have no meaning under the coarser-bump rule. A float is read as its text (0.3, 1.0), which drops a trailing zero (0.10 is 0.1): quote ten or more steps. The table names the unit outright — {"major": 1}, {"minor": 3}, {"patch": 2} — and can only ever carry one unit. An all-zero spelling ("0.0", {"minor": 0}) is a zero-count window in the unit of its last position: the distance check is off, but a clean bump of that unit or coarser is still required, so 1.2 → 1.2.1 still violates a zero-minor window.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default min_grace GraceWindowSpec

The dotted delta as a string or float, a one-key mapping from unit name to count, or an already-built window.

required

Returns:

Type Description GraceWindow

The strict window.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the specification is not of any accepted shape.

Examples:

>>> GraceWindow.parse("0.1")
GraceWindow(count=1, unit=<VersionBump.MINOR: 'minor'>)
>>> GraceWindow.parse("2.0")
GraceWindow(count=2, unit=<VersionBump.MAJOR: 'major'>)
>>> GraceWindow.parse({"patch": 3})
GraceWindow(count=3, unit=<VersionBump.PATCH: 'patch'>)
>>> GraceWindow.parse(0.3)
GraceWindow(count=3, unit=<VersionBump.MINOR: 'minor'>)

docs.title: deprecate.audit.DeprecationStatus
docs.text:
Bases: str, Enum

Lifecycle status labels used in the deprecation report's Current Status column.

Each member's value is the full display string (emoji + text) rendered in the table. Using a str enum means members compare equal to their string values and can be returned wherever a plain string is expected.

Members are declared from least to most urgent for readability, but this enum is not orderable by urgency: because each value starts with an emoji, the inherited str ordering operators (<, >) compare Unicode codepoints of those emoji, not deprecation urgency. Do not rely on status_a > status_b to mean "more urgent" — compare members explicitly (status is DeprecationStatus.PAST_REMOVAL_DATE). The ordering operators are overridden to raise TypeError so accidental comparisons fail loudly.

Examples:

>>> DeprecationStatus.ACTIVE_WARNING.value
'📢 Deprecation Active'
>>> DeprecationStatus.PAST_REMOVAL_DATE is DeprecationStatus.PAST_REMOVAL_DATE
True

docs.title: deprecate.TargetMode
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

Selects @deprecated behaviour when no callable replacement is provided.

Attributes:

Name Type Description AUTO

Decoration-time fallback that resolves the mode when target is omitted on the :func:~deprecate.deprecated front door -- "infer the mode from the configuration". It exists only to give an omitted target a sensible default; prefer passing an explicit mode (:attr:NOTIFY, :attr:ARGS_REMAP, :attr:ATTRS_REMAP) or a callable target so the intent is visible at the call site. Resolves before the wrapper/proxy is built: a mapping present selects :attr:ARGS_REMAP (args_mapping) or :attr:ATTRS_REMAP (attrs_mapping, class path); no mapping selects :attr:NOTIFY (callable path) or the proxy's unset target (class path). Passing AUTO explicitly to @deprecated is identical to omitting target; the strict factories (:func:~deprecate.routine.deprecated_callable, :func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_class) reject it with :class:TypeError -- they require an explicit mode. AUTO is never stored in :class:~deprecate._types.DeprecationConfig -- audit metadata always records the resolved mode.

NOTIFY

Notify-only deprecation -- warn on every call; original body executes unchanged. Replaces target=None. Combining an explicit NOTIFY with args_mapping, attrs_mapping, or args_extra is contradictory and emits a :class:UserWarning (the mapping/extras are ignored; :class:TypeError is planned in v1.0) -- with @deprecated, omit target instead to let :attr:AUTO pick the matching remap mode.

ARGS_REMAP

Deprecate argument names only -- warn only when deprecated argument names are passed; remaps kwargs via args_mapping before calling the original body. Replaces target=True. Selected automatically by :attr:AUTO when args_mapping is provided to @deprecated without an explicit target; using this mode without args_mapping emits a :class:UserWarning today, and :class:TypeError is planned in v1.0.

ATTRS_REMAP

Selective per-attribute deprecation -- warn only when a deprecated attribute alias listed in attrs_mapping is accessed; all other attribute access is forwarded silently. Proxy-specific mode: only valid for :func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_class; raises :class:TypeError on :func:~deprecate.deprecated decorated functions/methods. Analogous to :attr:ARGS_REMAP but for attribute access instead of call arguments. Selected automatically by :attr:AUTO when attrs_mapping is non-empty and no explicit target is provided.

Examples:

>>> from deprecate import TargetMode
>>> TargetMode.AUTO.value
'auto'
>>> TargetMode.NOTIFY.value
'notify'
>>> TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP.value
'args_remap'
>>> TargetMode.ATTRS_REMAP.value
'attrs_remap'

docs.title: deprecate.DeprecationProxy
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol, Generic[_T_co]

Public type produced by :func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_class / :func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_instance.

Documents the public contract that deprecated proxies satisfy:

  • __wrapped__ points back to the source object/class for static-analysis tools (Sphinx, mypy, IDEs).
  • __deprecation_config__ carries :class:DeprecationConfig metadata consumed by audit tools; __deprecated__ is a PEP-702-conformant message string.
  • Attribute, item, and call access is transparently forwarded to the wrapped source.

The type parameter T describes the instance type returned by calling the proxy (i.e. the target type for class-forwarding proxies). It is purely a static affordance: every runtime instance of :class:~deprecate.proxy._DeprecatedProxy passes isinstance(proxy, DeprecationProxy), including a proxy over a dict or a plain class that carries no __call__ or __getitem__ (a proxy carries only the protocols its wrapped object supports, so the proxy class is registered with this Protocol rather than matched member by member).

Protocol vs implementation

DeprecationProxy (public, this Protocol) describes the contract; :class:~deprecate.proxy._DeprecatedProxy (private) is the concrete runtime class that satisfies it. Annotate against the former, never import the latter.

Static-typing scope

This Protocol is the type to annotate against; it is not what the public functions declare as their return type. deprecated_instance returns the concrete :class:~deprecate.proxy._DeprecatedProxy, whose forwarded dunders (int(), with, await, ...) a narrow Protocol would hide from type checkers; annotate an instance proxy as DeprecationProxy[T] to name the type calling it produces. deprecated_class types a class alias as a class instead: deprecated_class(target=NewCls, ...)(OldCls) is type[NewCls] whichever class it wraps, and without a class target the alias keeps the wrapped class's own type. The @deprecated_class(...) decorator form is read as the class statement by mypy, while pyright applies the same return type as the call form. A class alias is therefore not assignable to DeprecationProxy. To reach the proxy-only attributes of a class alias statically, use :func:get_deprecation_config, or cast(DeprecationProxy[Any], OldCls) at the one site that needs them.

isinstance only

This is a data Protocol (it declares attributes, not just methods), so only isinstance is supported at runtime. issubclass(SomeType, DeprecationProxy) raises :class:TypeError, as it does for every @runtime_checkable Protocol with non-method members.

Example

from deprecate import deprecated_class, DeprecationProxy class NewColor: ... def init(self, code: int) -> None: ... self.code = code @deprecated_class(target=NewColor, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0", stream=None) ... class OldColor: ... pass isinstance(OldColor, DeprecationProxy) True OldColor.wrapped is OldColor.wrapped # breadcrumb back to the source class True

An instance proxy is where the type parameter pays off — spelled out as DeprecationProxy[NewColor], calling the proxy is typed as producing a NewColor:

from deprecate import deprecated_instance def make_color(code: int) -> NewColor: ... return NewColor(code) legacy_factory: DeprecationProxy[NewColor] = deprecated_instance( ... make_color, name="legacy_factory", deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0", stream=None ... ) isinstance(legacy_factory(1), NewColor) True

docs.text: Forward attribute access (e.g. OldColor.RED -> NewColor.RED).

docs.text: Forward item access (e.g. proxy['key'] -> source['key']).

docs.title: deprecate.get_deprecation_config(obj)
docs.text:
Return the :class:~deprecate._types.DeprecationConfig metadata attached to obj, if any.

This is the supported external read path for a wrapper's deprecation metadata, replacing direct obj.__deprecated__ access: since v0.13, __deprecated__ holds a plain PEP-702-conformant message string, not the config object — see the v0.12-to-v0.13 migration guide.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default obj Any

Any object to inspect — a @deprecated-wrapped function/method, a class or instance proxy from :func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_class / :func:~deprecate.proxy.deprecated_instance, or a module deprecated via :func:~deprecate.module.deprecated_module.

required

Returns:

Type Description Optional[DeprecationConfig]

The attached :class:~deprecate._types.DeprecationConfig, or None when obj carries no pyDeprecate

Optional[DeprecationConfig]

metadata.

Examples:

>>> from deprecate import deprecated, get_deprecation_config
>>> def new_func(): pass
>>> @deprecated(target=new_func, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0")
... def old_func(): pass
>>> get_deprecation_config(old_func).target is new_func
True
>>> get_deprecation_config(new_func) is None
True

docs.title: deprecate.utils.void(*args, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Empty function that accepts any arguments and returns None.

This helper function is used to silence IDE warnings about unused parameters in deprecated functions where the body is never executed (calls are forwarded to a target function). It's purely a convenience for developers.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default *args Any

Any positional arguments (ignored).

() **kwargs Any

Any keyword arguments (ignored).

{}

Returns:

Type Description Any

None always.

Example

from deprecate import deprecated, void

def new_func(x: int) -> int: ... return x * 2

@deprecated(target=new_func, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0") ... def old_func(x: int) -> int: ... void(x) # Silences IDE warning about unused 'x' ... # This line is never reached - call forwarded to new_func

Note

This function has no runtime effect - it's purely for developer convenience. You can also use pass or just a docstring instead of calling void().

docs.title: deprecate.utils.assert_no_warnings(warning_type=None, match=None)
docs.text:
Context manager asserting that no warnings are raised — the inverse of pytest.warns().

Useful for testing that refactored code properly avoids deprecated functionality or that new implementations don't trigger warnings.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default warning_type Optional[type[Warning]]

The warning type that must NOT be raised (e.g., :class:FutureWarning, :class:DeprecationWarning). If None, asserts that no warnings of any type are raised.

None match Optional[str]

If given, only fail if a warning message contains this string. If None, fails on any warning of the specified type.

None

Raises:

Type Description AssertionError

If a warning of the specified type (and optionally matching the message pattern) was raised during the context.

Example Note

This context manager is particularly useful in pytest for testing that refactored code properly uses new APIs without triggering deprecation warnings.

docs.title: Assert new function doesn't trigger FutureWarning
docs.text: import warnings def new_func(x: int) -> int: ... return x * 2 with assert_no_warnings(FutureWarning): ... result = new_func(42) result 84

docs.title: Assert NO warnings at all are raised
docs.text: def clean_function(): ... pass with assert_no_warnings(): ... clean_function()

docs.title: Only fail if warning message matches pattern
docs.text: def some_function(): ... warnings.warn("deprecated feature", FutureWarning)

docs.title: Passes because warning contains "feature", not "other"
docs.text: with assert_no_warnings(FutureWarning, match="other"): ... some_function()

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • deprecated_instance accepts keyword-only target, args_mapping and attrs_mapping. The old name can now serve a replacement object, rename keyword arguments when the object is called, and deprecate selected attributes, as deprecated_class does. (#263)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• args_mapping / args_extra on a non-callable object emit UserWarning and mark the config misconfigured. The mapping is inert at runtime and audit reports the proxy with misconfigured_target=True. (#263)
  • Misconfiguration warnings name the factory. The message says whether deprecated_instance or deprecated_class was called. (#263)
  • copy.copy of a proxy shallow-copies a plain data replacement. Top-level writes through a successful copy do not reach the original replacement; if copying raises, the replacement remains shared. Nested mutable values stay shared. (#263)
  • Audit treats a deprecated data proxy target as a TARGET chain and reports data targets by type; callable ARGS_REMAP targets are STACKED chains. (#263)

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
CLI & CI

  • --static mode for pydeprecate expiry and pydeprecate policy, and the pydeprecate-expiry-static / pydeprecate-policy-static pre-commit hooks. --static reads the package source with ast and imports nothing from it, so a package can be audited without its runtime dependencies installed. Recognized wrappers with resolvable settings are checked; recognized unresolved forms produce a pydeprecate gap: not statically resolvable line without changing the exit code unless --strict is set. Some forms are invisible without a gap, including wrappers created in loops or through getattr, importlib or exec; bare target names imported from outside the package can also be misclassified. See the CLI guide for the full limitations. The two -static hooks run the same checks from the shipped .pre-commit-hooks.yaml, and the --report-json record carries a new mode field, "static" or "import". check, chains, all and status have no static mode and exit 2 with --static. (#264)
  • --strict fails a run that recorded a gap. --strict, or strict = true in [tool.pydeprecate], makes any pydeprecate gap: line exit 1 on every subcommand but status. A typed --strict with --exit-zero exits 2; a typed --exit-zero overrides a strict = true that only pyproject.toml sets. (#265)
  • --ignore and --baseline accept known findings. --ignore takes module:symbol or rule:module:symbol globs and --baseline a --report-json file with a findings list; matched findings are not printed, counted or gated on, and only ids a baseline itself suppressed carry over when it is regenerated. (#265)
  • --report-json records every finding, plus gate and mode. Each finding has an id, rule, level, message and location. The report layout stays schema 1: the new keys are additive, so a 0.15 reader still reads the file. (#265)
  • Every CLI subcommand audits several paths in one run. pydeprecate check src/ lib/ takes any number of paths; the GitHub Action path input takes one path per line. (#266)
  • pydeprecate all --gate=policy fails on policy violations. --gate (or gate = ["policy"] in [tool.pydeprecate]) takes a comma-separated list over check, expiry, policy and chains; only policy changes the exit code, and it counts the violations of the same scan. An unknown check exits 2. Without it all keeps reporting policy violations without failing on them. (#266)
  • --report-sarif FILE writes SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning. One result per active finding, keyed by finding id; suppressed findings are omitted and gaps become tool notifications. Available on every subcommand except status. (#266)
  • The GitHub Action gains fail-on-gap and sarif inputs, step outputs and finding annotations. fail-on-gap maps to --strict and sarif to --report-sarif; the step outputs are exit-code, findings, errors, warnings, gaps, suppressed, report-json and sarif-file. Each finding becomes an annotation on its wrapper's line, at most 10 per level per step, with the rest counted in one notice. (#266)

Audit API

  • find_deprecation_wrappers_static() audits a package from source without importing it. It reads the source with ast, as --static does, and returns a frozen StaticScanResult with wrappers, gaps and the version resolved without imports. validate_deprecation_expiry, validate_deprecation_policy and generate_deprecation_table accept the result in place of a module, so a script or docs build can audit a package whose dependencies are missing. Rows are read from source and carry stand-in targets, so read .gaps before treating a result as clean. (#268)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• A second positional argument on expiry, all and status is a path first; read as a version it is deprecated. With two positionals, the second is read as the version only when it names no path or findable module and parses as a version; that spelling prints a stderr notice and is removed in 1.0. Pass --version instead; passing both exits 2. (#266)
  • Version detection stops at the nearest project. For a path scan, the nearest pyproject.toml with a [project] table owns version detection even when its version cannot be resolved; an ancestor project's version is not used. If the remaining metadata and package-version sources also fail, expiry reports a version not resolved gap. (#264)
  • An operand after -- is always a path, never the legacy positional version. pydeprecate expiry -- src/pkg 2.0 now scans 2.0 as a second path instead of reading it as --version 2.0; pass --version 2.0. (#266)
  • A callable-target proxy with args_mapping shares one warning budget per call. deprecated_class and deprecated_instance with a callable target and args_mapping now emit one call-level warning per call instead of one per renamed keyword; dataclass auto-expanded aliases keep a separate budget for each deprecated keyword. (#273)
  • read_only=True proxies also block sort, reverse, popitem, difference_update, intersection_update and symmetric_difference_update. They raise AttributeError instead of changing the wrapped list, dict or set, which brings the guarded method names from 10 to 16; a custom method with one of these names is blocked too. (#273)
  • deprecated_module with a message_template no longer warns about a missing deprecated_in. The template writes the whole message, as it does for @deprecated; stream=None still warns. (#273)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A keyword named like a positional-only parameter stays a keyword when a call is rewritten. For a callable declaring **kwargs, such as def f(x=1, /, flag=None, **kwargs), a renamed or forwarded call like f(old_flag=1, x=99) now passes x=99 into kwargs and keeps the default x, as the undecorated call does, instead of moving it into the positional slot. Applies to @deprecated and to deprecated_class / deprecated_instance proxies with args_mapping. (#263)
  • Matrix audit tables have one column per release. generate_deprecation_table(..., style="matrix") and the CLI matrix output merge the spellings 1.0, v1.0 and 1.0.0 of one release into a single column, headed by the shortest spelling. Without packaging only spellings that differ by the v prefix merge. (#262)
  • validate_deprecation_expiry(<module path>) without a version surfaces the package's real import error. The module path is now imported before the version lookup, so a package whose own import fails raises its actual exception instead of "Could not determine version". A degenerate module path such as an empty name raises importlib's own error. (#262)
  • Unparsed matrix columns are ordered by their displayed header text. Version strings that are not PEP 440 releases come after the parsed releases, now sorted by the v-prefixed header as rendered instead of the raw string, so columns such as next and vlegacy swap order (vlegacy | vnext). A committed matrix table that contains such columns re-renders with the new order. (#262)
  • Audit names ATTRS_REMAP and ARGS_REMAP misconfigurations correctly. The misconfigured-target finding text and details now say which contradiction the wrapper has, such as an ATTRS_REMAP without attrs_mapping or one with an ignored args_mapping; rule, level and exit code are unchanged. (#273)

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • The empty cli extra is removed. The pydeprecate command has needed no dependency since v0.15, so pip install 'pyDeprecate[audit]' now covers every command. pip install 'pyDeprecate[cli]' still installs the package, with pip's warning that the extra does not exist; the hooks manifest and the GitHub Action install pyDeprecate[audit]. (#269)

docs.title: [0.15.0] — 2026-11-09 — Scoped fatal deprecations, a dependency-free CLI, & CI integrations
Added
docs.text:
Fatal deprecations

  • Scoped fatal deprecations — as_exceptions() context manager. with deprecate.as_exceptions(): makes deprecations fatal for one block and restores the previous setting on exit, including when the block raises, so nested scopes compose; as_exceptions(False) exempts a block from a strict run, while a wrapper's own as_exception=True stays fatal. The scope is held in a ContextVar, so it is local to the current thread and asyncio task, and the global deprecate.AS_EXCEPTIONS is not modified. Also usable as a decorator on synchronous functions; async def, generator and async-generator functions are rejected with TypeError at decoration, and a non-bool flag (including a bare @as_exceptions) raises TypeError at the call. (#240, #253)

CLI & CI

  • pre-commit hooks. The repository now ships .pre-commit-hooks.yaml, so other projects can run the CLI as a hook (repo: https://github.com/Borda/pyDeprecate) without wrapping it in a repo: local entry. There is one hook id per subcommand — pydeprecate-check, pydeprecate-policy, pydeprecate-expiry, pydeprecate-chains, pydeprecate-all, plus pydeprecate as an alias of pydeprecate-check — so args only carries flags, plus the package path when it is not under src/. The scan imports the audited package, so packages with runtime dependencies should keep a local hook; the audit guide covers both recipes. (#243)
  • Composite GitHub Action. Run the audit CLI as a single workflow step in the job's own Python, with inputs for the subcommand, package path, extra flags, advisory mode (exit-zero), installation, and an optional deprecation status table in the job summary. By default, the action installs pyDeprecate[cli,audit] from the action ref; install: false keeps the version already installed by the job. Set up Python and install the audited package's dependencies before running the action. (#245)
  • Scan output files.
  • --report-json FILE on every CLI subcommand. Writes the run's machine-readable record — the deprecation table of the scan that ran, plus every audit gap with its kind, detail and a remedy hint — on exit 0 or 1; a usage error writes none, and a failed write never changes the exit code. The GitHub Action builds its gap annotations and job summary from it, so a single-gate summary now covers exactly the gate's scan. (#245)
  • pydeprecate all --output FILE. all can now also save the deprecation table it appends, as status --output does; a failure to write the file is reported but never changes the exit code. (#245)
  • include_members on every audit validator and CLI gate. validate_deprecation_chains and validate_mapping_compatibility accept include_members: bool = True, the switch find_deprecation_wrappers already had, and check, expiry, policy, chains and all accept --no-include-members (previously status only) to skip class members. (#249, #252)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
Call forwarding & decoration

  • functools.partial, partialmethod and singledispatchmethod sources are rejected at decoration. @deprecated and deprecated_callable() raise TypeError for these objects, including a named partial (one given a __name__ through functools.update_wrapper) that earlier releases accepted and forwarded with a wrong result. Wrap the object in a plain def that calls it and decorate that def. (#250)
  • An empty-string args_mapping value keeps the old argument name under @deprecated. args_mapping={"old_arg": ""} now passes old_arg through under its original name (the notice still fires), matching deprecated_class; only None drops an argument. On 0.14 @deprecated dropped an argument mapped to "" like one mapped to None — map it to None if you relied on that. (#251)
  • Forwarding to a classmethod accepts any receiver name. The source no longer needs a first parameter named cls: klass, mcs or a target receiver such as kls forward the same way, and a source with no leading positional parameter, or a later parameter named like the target's receiver, is rejected with TypeError at decoration. A static or plain source that is given a non-class first argument now raises TypeError before the warning is emitted or the num_warns budget is spent. (#257)
  • Generator and async-generator wrappers preserve their callable kind and defer deprecation handling until iteration. inspect.isgeneratorfunction(wrapper) and inspect.isasyncgenfunction(wrapper) now match the source, so frameworks such as pytest recognise deprecated yield fixtures. Unlike the eager call-time warnings introduced in 0.9.0, the warning, num_warns budget, skip_if evaluation, argument binding and an as_exception / as_exceptions() error now resolve on the first next() / __anext__() step; a generator that is never iterated never warns or spends the budget. Move pytest.warns() and pytest.raises() assertions around the first iteration, and keep as_exceptions() active at that step rather than only around generator creation. (#256)
  • Warnings that reported a deprecate frame now point at the caller. Call-time warnings already named the user's call site; the remaining ones, notably the inner warning of a stacked deprecation chain, now carry the caller's line and module too. A warning filter keyed on module="deprecate" that matched those warnings no longer does, so they surface — and raise under -W error — so key filters on the calling code's module instead. (#250)
  • A custom stream is called exactly once. pyDeprecate reads its signature before the call and never retries after a TypeError. A stream that declares **kwargs receives stacklevel= and must accept or drop it: forward it to warnings.warn or logging.warning, not to print(msg, **kwargs), which raises TypeError; declare def sink(msg) to receive the message alone. A bare (*args, **kwargs) functools.wraps pass-through is classified by the callable it wraps, and a stream whose only parameter is named stacklevel receives the message alone. (#250)
  • Multi-argument rename warnings name only the arguments still within their budget. With num_warns=1, a call using old_a and then a call using old_a and old_b no longer re-lists old_a in the second message. (#251)
  • A class decorated with @deprecated gets its dispatch notice once under concurrent decoration. The one-time notice is claimed under a lock, and the set of remembered classes is capped at 4096 keys, evicting the oldest, so an evicted class may warn again. (#251)

Proxies

  • Function proxies bind like methods, and only plain functions do. A deprecated_instance over a plain function or a @deprecated wrapper stored as a class attribute passes the instance as self, so Model().scale(2) reaches the function with the instance; use staticmethod(deprecated_instance(...)) for static-style access. Any other callable — functools.partial, a bound method, a builtin or a Cython binding callable — is served unbound and silent on every Python version, so a deprecated partial class attribute no longer warns through Python's own binding. (#250)
  • Proxies carry only the protocols of the wrapped object or its replacement. A deprecated_instance or deprecated_class proxy now allocates a cached subclass with only the optional dunders the served object supports, so a deprecated dict is no longer callable(), an Iterator, os.PathLike, Awaitable or AsyncIterable, and a protocol the object disables (__iter__ = None, __contains__ = None) stays disabled instead of falling back. The set is fixed when the proxy is created. Visible differences: a missing-protocol error names _DeprecatedProxy; in and reversed() that fall back through __iter__ now warn; type(proxy) is _DeprecatedProxy is False, so use isinstance(proxy, DeprecationProxy); and the generated proxy subclasses cannot be pickled by reference. (#257)
  • When a proxy warns or refuses.
  • Fatal mode refuses reads before they run. Under as_exception=True or strict mode, a subscript, iteration, round(), a unary operator or a mapped attribute read raises DeprecatedError before touching the wrapped object, so a missing key adds no defaultdict entry and a mapped getter or user __iter__ never runs. (#250)
  • next() warns before advancing. The warning is delivered before the wrapped iterator moves, so a FutureWarning raised as an error, or a failing stream, no longer consumes an item. The call that raises StopIteration now counts as a use and spends the num_warns budget when it is the first. In-place operators and defaultdict subscripts still warn after they run, so their effect stays if delivery fails. (#250)
  • Async operations warn when the awaitable is obtained. __await__ and __anext__ deliver the warning when they hand out the underlying awaitable, so a later failure or exhaustion inside await or async for still consumes the warning budget. When the warning itself fails (an error filter, a raising stream), the coroutine the proxy created is closed instead of being left un-awaited, and an async generator stays usable. (#250)
  • Context entry unwinds when warning delivery fails. If the warning raises on with proxy: or async with proxy:, the acquired sync or async context is exited, with the delivery error preserved even when the exit returns a suppression value. (#250)
  • Item writes and in-place writes honour skip_if. With skip_if active, proxy[key] = value, del proxy[key] and in-place operators write to the wrapped object and the read-only guard does not apply; item writes never warn. (#250)
  • %(source_path)s in proxy message templates is module-qualified. For deprecated_class and deprecated_instance a custom message_template now receives <module>.<name> when the proxy wraps a class or a plain function, and <source_path>.<attr> for attribute warnings; the default messages are unchanged. (#251)

CLI

  • Argument parsing.
  • CLI built on argparse, without fire or rich. The pydeprecate command uses only the standard library, so pip install pyDeprecate is enough to run it; the cli extra is kept, empty, so pip install 'pyDeprecate[cli]' keeps working. Option values are always strings, boolean flags are negated with --no-flag (the older --noflag spelling still works, unlisted in --help), options may be spelled with dashes or underscores but never abbreviated, arguments after -- are always operands, and pydeprecate <subcommand> --help lists each subcommand's options. Spellings only Fire accepted now exit 2 with argparse's message: a quoted literal such as --version '"0.10"', a list literal in --exclude (pass comma-separated patterns), a table in --min-grace (write it in pyproject.toml), --path=pkg, short flags such as -r, an empty --report-json=, and the version given both as the second argument and as --version. (#252)
  • Stricter validation. A boolean flag now accepts only true, false, 1 or 0 (case-insensitive) in both --flag value and --flag=value forms, and any other value exits 2; a second positional path for check, policy or chains, and private --_* options such as --_advisory, exit 2 as well. Scanning a directory that holds several top-level packages (for example a repository root with mypkg/ and tests/) now fails with a non-zero exit and a "contains multiple packages" error instead of passing silently on an empty scan; src-layout and single-package roots resolve as before. (#243)
  • CLI exit codes. check and all now exit 1 on misconfigured targets (target=False, TargetMode.NOTIFY with an args_mapping, attrs_mapping or args_extra it ignores, TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP without an args_mapping) and on inner-order @property @deprecated wrappers, which they used to pass. Exit 3 is new: pydeprecate: scan error: … when the scanned package itself cannot be imported or its module-level code calls sys.exit(), and pydeprecate: internal error: … for a bug in the CLI; both used to exit 1, like findings. --exit-zero masks neither 2 nor 3, and neither writes a --report-json file. A name that is neither an existing path nor an importable module, a single .py file and a directory holding several packages exit 2. status exits 2 for an invalid --version (was a raw error, exit 1) and an unknown --style (was a silent fallback, exit 0). The GitHub Action annotates exit 3 as a scan or internal error. (#252)
  • Audit gaps on stderr. When part of the audit did not run, the CLI now prints an unwrapped stderr line starting with pydeprecate gap: <kind>: — one pydeprecate gap: module not audited: <module>: <error> line per submodule that failed to import (printed whatever warnings filters the audited package installs, unlike the audit: skipped warning), plus version not resolved, version not PEP 440, packaging missing and nested files not audited. These lines replace the earlier free-form Skipping … / Could not scan … / version and packaging advisories; tooling reads the same gaps from --report-json. (#245)

Modules, imports & packaging

  • import deprecate no longer loads the audit tooling. The audit names, including the legacy aliases, resolve lazily on first access, which roughly halves import time, and calls whose warning budget is spent take a cheaper path. deprecate.proxy is now a package; its public import paths and pickle identity are unchanged, but inspect.getsource on the proxy classes no longer finds their source. (#251)
  • Star-import surface follows __all__. deprecate.utils, deprecate.routine, deprecate.messaging, deprecate.module, deprecate.deprecation, the deprecate.proxy package with its submodules and the deprecate.docstring modules now define __all__, so from deprecate.<module> import * pulls in only the listed public names. Import the public API from the top-level deprecate package. (#253)
  • deprecated_module(stream=None) now warns at the call. The stream default is a separate sentinel, so omitting it keeps delivering through warnings.warn silently, while an explicit stream=None still delivers through warnings.warn but raises a FutureWarning at the deprecated_module(...) call: from v1.0 it silences the module warning like every other entry point, and the num_warns default changes from -1 to 1. The v0.14.0 docstring ("Pass None (default)") described the old default. (#253)
  • DeprecationWrapperInfo.empty_mapping and identity_mapping warn with FutureWarning. The deprecated aliases are wrapped with pyDeprecate's own @deprecated, so reading them emits a FutureWarning on every access instead of a DeprecationWarning; update any filter keyed on the old category. Removal stays at v1.0. (#253)
  • Package metadata in pyproject.toml. Static metadata moved from setup.py into [project]; setuptools stays the build backend and setup.py only renders the PyPI long description. The wheel metadata drops the author email, states the license as License-Expression: Apache-2.0 with its License-File, and lists the homepage as Project-URL: Homepage instead of Home-page. (#252)

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text:
• DeprecationConfig call-time cache fields. target_positional_only, target_positional_only_order, source_positional_only, source_positional_only_order, source_var_positional_prefix, target_all_param_names, target_accepts_var_positional and target_accepts_var_keyword are internal and leave DeprecationConfig in v1.0; read the public fields through get_deprecation_config(obj). Announced in the docs only; reading them emits no warning. (#253)
  • Internal helpers with public-looking names. deprecate.utils.get_func_arguments_types_defaults and the names in deprecate.docstring.inject are internal (left out of each module's __all__) and gain a leading underscore in v1.0; reading them emits no warning. Use inspect.signature and update_docstring=True instead. (#253)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
Call forwarding & signatures

  • Callable forwarding and proxy edge cases. Calls that need no forwarding reach the source with the caller's own positional and keyword arguments, and warning state is cleaned up if a custom stream raises. A warning that fails to deliver no longer spends the proxy's warn budget, reads and other warning data-use proxy operations evaluate skip_if once (calls and writes may still consult it more than once), and a deprecated functools.partial class attribute is no longer bound or warned about by Python. Audit tables and --report-json name functools.partial and callable-instance targets the way the runtime warning does instead of printing an address-bearing repr. (#250)
  • *args sources.
  • Explicit new argument name wins. When a source declares *args and a call passes both the deprecated and the new name, the new-name value is forwarded whatever the keyword order, as the collision warning says. (#251)
  • args_extra is injected. TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP with args_extra on a source declaring *args now injects args_extra for a caller who already uses the new argument names. (#251)
  • Forwarding keeps the target's own signature error, and docless classes stay docless. When forwarded keywords need validating, the original introspection error is raised instead of a misleading keyword error, and a deprecated class without a docstring no longer exposes internal proxy text as its __doc__. (#251)
  • Decorated callables can be garbage-collected. A signature cache kept every decorated callable alive; it is gone, and a source default whose __ne__ misbehaves (for example an array) no longer crashes a forwarded call. (#251)

Proxies & concurrency

  • Instances of a class deprecated in place pickle and load as the original class. deprecated_class registers a copyreg reducer so pickle, copy and deepcopy of an instance no longer fail on the proxy bound to the class name; loading rebuilds the original class without a warning. A class that defines or inherits its own __reduce_ex__, a redirect and a stacked deprecation keep their own reduction, and the class object itself still cannot be pickled. (#257)
  • One misconfiguration notice under threads. The one-time UserWarning for a misconfigured wrapper is claimed under the wrapper's lock, so concurrent first calls emit it exactly once. (#251)
  • Module redirect guard no longer reports false cycles. Concurrent asyncio tasks keep separate guards, a thread started in a copy of a resolving context no longer mistakes its own lookup of the same name for a cycle, and the guard expires when the original lookup finishes, so later work in a copied context resolves the name normally. A real cycle on the same thread still raises AttributeError. (#251)

CLI & audit

  • Version resolution.
  • One resolver for every gate. expiry, all, status and the JSON table resolve the version the same way (local pyproject.toml, installed metadata, distribution mapping, then __version__), so all and status no longer report version not resolved for a package that only declares __version__, and validate_deprecation_expiry / generate_deprecation_table resolve packages whose distribution name differs from the import name. (#246)
  • Standalone pydeprecate expiry. It retains the top-level package's __version__ fallback when project and installed metadata cannot resolve a version, so overdue wrappers in uninstalled checkouts still exit 1. A genuinely unresolved version now prints one version not resolved gap instead of two, and an auto-detected version that is not PEP 440 skips the check with a gap (exit 0) instead of crashing with ValueError, as pydeprecate all already did. (#245, #246)
  • Every subcommand scans a plain directory of modules. expiry and chains raised ValueError on a directory of top-level modules that check already scanned; the scanned package no longer sees the CLI's own sys.argv, the scan header names the file it imported from, and an import resolved outside the scanned directory is reported as an other copy audited gap. (#248)
  • Boolean flags before the path. A boolean flag placed before the path (pydeprecate check --exit-zero src/mypackage) no longer swallows the path, and policy --message-required / --no-message-required now work before the path too instead of exiting 2. (#243, #252)
  • --version 0.10 keeps its trailing zero. The CLI read it as the number 0.1, so expiry, all and status compared against the wrong release and could pass overdue wrappers. (#252)
  • A submodule that calls sys.exit() no longer ends a recursive audit scan. find_deprecation_wrappers skips it with the audit: skipped <module> warning, as for any other import failure, and the CLI reports a module not audited gap; an unguarded __main__.py used to end the scan with the module's own exit code. (#252)

docs.title: [0.14.0] — 2026-10-06 — Fatal deprecations, PEP 702 static-checker support, & module warning budgets
Added
docs.text:
• Opt-in audit discovery for PEP 702-only deprecations. find_deprecation_wrappers(..., include_pep702=True) lists symbols marked only with warnings.deprecated or typing_extensions.deprecated. Each row keeps a shape api_type (callable, class, class method, staticmethod, ...) like any other row, and carries the decorator's message in the new DeprecationWrapperInfo.pep702_message field, which is None on every pyDeprecate row. Only symbols the scanned package defines are listed: no inherited class members, no __new__/__init_subclass__ hooks the decorator installs, no instances of a deprecated class, a class bound under a second name lists its PEP 702 member rows once, under the binding named like the class (its pyDeprecate member rows still appear under each name), and no imports from other top-level packages. The default scan and existing audit gates remain unchanged. (#237)
