docs.text:
For deprecated_module(), explicit stream=None historically meant warnings.warn, whereas other entry points treat it as silence. It still delivers warnings today, with a FutureWarning announcing the change at the deprecated_module(...) call.

Q: I passed stream=None to deprecated_module() expecting silence, as with @deprecated, but the module warning still appears, and a FutureWarning now fires at the deprecated_module(...) call itself.

The default is now a separate sentinel, displayed as <warnings.warn> by help(). Omitting stream preserves current behavior without that notice.

Changes in v1.0

In v1.0, stream=None silences module warnings and the num_warns default changes from -1 to 1.

  • Omit stream to keep warning on access.
  • Pass num_warns=-1 explicitly if every access must keep warning after v1.0.
  • To silence module deprecations today, use a warnings filter or a custom stream that discards the message.

docs.title: Why do pytest, Sphinx, or my IDE trigger warnings on a deprecated module?
docs.text:
That is expected in Mode 1 and Mode 2. deprecated_module() overrides the module's __getattribute__, so any public attribute probe invokes the warning path even when the access comes from tooling rather than your own code. Standard warning filters can suppress repeated display; custom streams can still observe every permitted delivery.

Test and documentation tools often call getattr(), inspect plugin metadata, or walk module attributes repeatedly during discovery.

Q: I only imported a deprecated module once, but pytest collection, Sphinx autodoc, or my IDE/linter triggers many FutureWarnings. Why?

If that noise is expected in tests, scope it in test config with warnings.filterwarnings instead of suppressing warnings globally:

# tests/conftest.py
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=FutureWarning, message=r"The `old_module` module was deprecated")

Replace old_module with the deprecated module's import path. Escape dots in dotted paths, such as pkg\.old_module.

Filter by message=, rather than module=. The warning is attributed to the module accessing the deprecated one, so module=r"^old_module$" never matches.

The example matches the start of the built-in notice: "The old_module module was deprecated since v...". With a custom message_template, match the start of that text instead. This silences noisy test-collection introspection while keeping the warning visible elsewhere.

docs.title: AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'target' after upgrading to v0.13
docs.text:
Since v0.13, __deprecated__ holds a plain PEP 702-conformant message string instead of the internal DeprecationConfig object. This matches warnings.deprecated and typing_extensions.deprecated.

Q: Code that used to read wrapper.__deprecated__.target (or .deprecated_in, or checked isinstance(wrapper.__deprecated__, DeprecationConfig)) now raises AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute .... What changed?

Before v0.13, PEP-702-aware tooling received a DeprecationConfig repr where a message string belonged. The change fixes that collision for IDE hover, pyright, and mypy.

The config object moved to __deprecation_config__. Read it through the public get_deprecation_config(obj) helper rather than accessing either attribute directly.

The helper also supports legacy objects whose __deprecated__ still holds a config. Migrated code therefore works across mixed-version installs, including objects built before v0.13.

from deprecate import deprecated, get_deprecation_config


# NEW API — new_func is the replacement API.
def new_func(x: int) -> int:
    return x * 2


# DEPRECATED API — old_func forwards to new_func.
@deprecated(target=new_func, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0")
def old_func(x: int) -> int:  # warns: nothing — decoration only, no call yet
    pass


print(isinstance(old_func.__deprecated__, str))
print(get_deprecation_config(old_func).target is new_func)
Output: isinstance(...) and get_deprecation_config(...).target 
True
True

Affects every wrapper kind — functions, methods, class proxies (deprecated_class), instance proxies (deprecated_instance), and modules (deprecated_module). See the v0.12-to-v0.13 migration guide for the full list of affected reads.

docs.title: How do I type-annotate the object returned by deprecated_class / deprecated_instance?
docs.text:
A class alias is typed as the class it forwards to; an instance proxy is annotated with the public DeprecationProxy.

Q: What type do type checkers see for the result of deprecated_class(...) and deprecated_instance(...), and what should I annotate against?

deprecated_class is typed to return its target. For example, RetryConfig = deprecated_class(target=RetryPolicy, ...)(RetryPolicy) has type type[RetryPolicy]. It needs no annotation, and isinstance(x, RetryConfig) narrows to RetryPolicy.

Without a class target, an alias using only args_mapping or attrs_mapping keeps the wrapped class's type.

Annotate deprecated_instance results with public DeprecationProxy, never private _DeprecatedProxy. Use DeprecationProxy[T] when calling the proxy produces a T:

from dataclasses import dataclass
from deprecate import DeprecationProxy, deprecated_class, deprecated_instance


# NEW API — RetryPolicy is the replacement API.
@dataclass
class RetryPolicy:
    attempts: int


# class alias — typed `type[RetryPolicy]`, no annotation needed
# DEPRECATED API — RetryConfig forwards to RetryPolicy.
RetryConfig = deprecated_class(target=RetryPolicy, deprecated_in="1.4", remove_in="2.0")(RetryPolicy)


def default_policy() -> RetryPolicy:
    return RetryPolicy(3)


# instance proxy — annotated with the public protocol, so `legacy_default()` is typed `RetryPolicy`
legacy_default: DeprecationProxy[RetryPolicy] = deprecated_instance(
    default_policy, name="legacy_default", deprecated_in="1.4", remove_in="2.0"
)

print(isinstance(RetryConfig(3), RetryPolicy))  # warns: FutureWarning
print(legacy_default().attempts)  # warns: FutureWarning
Output: isinstance(RetryConfig(3), RetryPolicy); legacy_default().attempts 
True
3

A class alias remains a proxy at runtime: isinstance(RetryConfig, DeprecationProxy) is True. Its proxy-only attributes, __wrapped__ and __deprecation_config__, are invisible on type[RetryPolicy].

Read them using get_deprecation_config(RetryConfig) or inspect.unwrap(RetryConfig). Alternatively, use cast(DeprecationProxy[Any], RetryConfig) at the site needing them. See Classes → Type annotations and static analysis for other checks against aliases.

issubclass raises TypeError

DeprecationProxy declares attributes (__wrapped__, __deprecated__), which makes it a data protocol. Python supports only isinstance for those: isinstance(obj, DeprecationProxy) works. issubclass(SomeType, DeprecationProxy) raises TypeError: Protocols with non-method members don't support issubclass().

This is a CPython rule for every runtime-checkable protocol with non-method members, not a pyDeprecate restriction.

docs.title: mypy reports errors on deprecated class aliases after upgrading
docs.text:
Before v0.14, pyDeprecate shipped no type information, so type checkers treated its objects as Any. Since v0.14, the package ships py.typed. Deprecated class aliases now have the forwarded class's type.

Q: After upgrading pyDeprecate, mypy reports new errors around deprecated_class aliases that used to pass. What changed?

Form Inferred type deprecated_class(target=New, ...)(Cls) type[New] deprecated_class(...)(Cls) without a class target type[Cls] @deprecated_class(...) class statement in mypy The class statement's type @deprecated_class(target=New, ...) in pyright The decorator's return type, type[New]

Common errors and fixes follow.

  • [assignment] on Old: DeprecationProxy[New] = deprecated_class(target=New, ...)(Cls). The alias is type[New], not a proxy type. Drop the annotation; the alias already has the replacement's type.
  • [attr-defined] on Old.__wrapped__ or Old.__deprecation_config__ — proxy-only attributes are invisible on the class type. Use get_deprecation_config(Old), inspect.unwrap(Old), or cast(DeprecationProxy[Any], Old).
  • [call-arg] or [attr-defined] on an old keyword or attribute name. args_mapping and attrs_mapping can accept names absent from the alias's class type. This matches the decorator form's existing diagnostics. Keep old names in a legacy class body, or cast the alias as cast(DeprecationProxy[New], deprecated_class(...)(New)). That cast makes calls and attributes permissive, but isinstance against the alias no longer type-checks.
  • [valid-type] on def f(x: Old), or class Child(Old) in mypy. A call-form alias is a variable, which type checkers cannot accept as a type. Annotate or subclass the replacement class. In mypy, you can also use the decorator form, whose name is a class statement.

See Classes → Type annotations and static analysis.

docs.title: Sphinx / my IDE shows (*args, **kwargs) instead of my deprecated class's real signature
docs.text:
Every proxy exposes __wrapped__ and __signature__ to reach the wrapped object and its signature. Reading either emits no deprecation warning, keeping documentation builds and IDE hovers quiet.

Q: Autodoc renders the proxy rather than the wrapped class, or inspect.signature() on a deprecated alias returns something useless. How do I reach the original?

Attribute Points to Consumed by __wrapped__ the source class or object inspect.unwrap, Sphinx autodoc, griffe/mkdocstrings, IDEs __signature__ the source's signature inspect.signature, and tools that do not walk __wrapped__ 
import inspect
from dataclasses import dataclass
from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — RetryPolicy is the replacement API.
@dataclass
class RetryPolicy:
    attempts: int
    backoff: float = 1.0


# DEPRECATED API — RetryConfig forwards to RetryPolicy.
@deprecated_class(target=RetryPolicy, deprecated_in="1.4", remove_in="2.0")
@dataclass
class RetryConfig:
    attempts: int
    backoff: float = 1.0


print(inspect.unwrap(RetryConfig).__name__)
print(str(inspect.signature(RetryConfig)))
Output: inspect.unwrap(RetryConfig).__name__; str(inspect.signature(RetryConfig)) 
RetryConfig
(attempts: int, backoff: float = 1.0) -> None

If a tool still renders the proxy, point it at __wrapped__ explicitly.

Some objects have no introspectable signature. Examples include a plain dict passed to deprecated_instance() and C-level types. In these cases, __signature__ is None, rather than absent. Wrapping never fails because the source cannot be introspected.

docs.title: Why don't mypy, pyright, or my IDE flag functions deprecated with pyDeprecate?
docs.text:
Type checkers recognize deprecation only from a literal warnings.deprecated (Python 3.13+) or typing_extensions.deprecated decorator. They match its name, so runtime decorators, including pyDeprecate's, cannot supply this signal alone.

Q: My deprecated function warns at runtime, but the editor shows no strikethrough and mypy / pyright report nothing when I call it.

  1. Stack the PEP 702 decorator directly above pyDeprecate's: @warnings.deprecated("Usenew_nameinstead.", category=None) over @deprecated(...).
  2. Keep category=None to avoid two warnings per call.
  3. Write the message as a string literal. Mypy silently ignores constants and f-strings.
  4. Import the module instead of the name to avoid shadowing pyDeprecate's deprecated.
  5. Enable enable_error_code = ["deprecated"] in mypy or reportDeprecated = "error" for pyright in CI.

Over @deprecated_class(...), both mypy and pyright flag the old class name. See Functions → Static type checkers.

docs.title: Does the deprecation survive copy, deepcopy, and pickle?
docs.text:
Yes for copy.copy and copy.deepcopy: the result remains a proxy with deprecation warnings. Warning counters are snapshotted at copy time, and each copy keeps an independent counter.

Q: I copied (or pickled and restored) an object wrapped by deprecated_instance / deprecated_class — does the deprecation still apply to the copy?

Copy operations are silent because the protocol methods rebuild the proxy directly without attribute access. Warnings begin when the copy is used.

Pickling depends on the wrapped object

  • deprecated_instance proxies over plain objects, including dicts, lists, and custom objects, are fully picklable.
  • A deprecated_class alias itself commonly raises PicklingError when its proxy replaces the original class's module-level name. Pickle cannot find the original class by reference.
  • Instances of a class deprecated in place pickle and load as instances of the original class. Neither step warns.
  • This includes exception and OrderedDict subclasses. An exception raised in a process-pool worker therefore still reaches the parent.
  • A class with its own __reduce_ex__ keeps its own pickling. Members of an Enum deprecated in place therefore still raise PicklingError.
import copy
import pickle

from deprecate import deprecated_instance

# NEW API — the canonical settings object going forward
NEW_LIMITS = {"max_retries": 3}

# DEPRECATED API — `OLD_LIMITS` kept as a deprecated alias during the migration window
OLD_LIMITS = deprecated_instance(NEW_LIMITS, name="OLD_LIMITS", deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0")

restored = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(OLD_LIMITS))  # noqa: S301  # silent — pickling rebuilds the proxy, not a usage
duplicate = copy.deepcopy(OLD_LIMITS)  # silent

print(restored["max_retries"])  # warns: FutureWarning
print(duplicate["max_retries"])  # warns: FutureWarning — each copy has its own counter snapshotted from the original
Output: restored["max_retries"]; duplicate["max_retries"] 
3
3

docs.title: What do pickled instances of a class deprecated in place need to load?
docs.text:
The loading process needs pyDeprecate installed, and the class must remain deprecated in place when the payload loads.

Q: I pickle instances of a class deprecated in place (@deprecated_class with no replacement class) into a cache or a worker queue. What does the process that loads them need, and do the payloads survive upgrading pyDeprecate or removing the deprecation?

The class's module-level name holds the proxy, so the payload cannot name the class directly. Instead, it names a pyDeprecate rebuild helper together with the class's module and qualified name.

The helper is deprecate.proxy._rebuild_class_instance, _rebuild_class_instance_ex, or _rebuild_class_call.

  • Upgrading pyDeprecate is safe. The helper names belong to the pickle compatibility contract and stay unchanged across releases, allowing payloads to load in later releases. Before v0.15, pyDeprecate lacks these helpers and cannot load such payloads.
  • Removing the deprecation breaks loading. The helpers rebuild only a class whose name a deprecation proxy holds. Once the deprecation is gone and the name points at the plain class again, loading raises AttributeError: Cannot rebuild the pickled instance: ... is not a class deprecated in place.

To migrate stored instances:

  1. Load them while the deprecation remains in place.
  2. In the migrating process, set the module attribute back to the real class using inspect.unwrap(OldClass).
  3. Pickle the loaded instances again.

Preserve the class's import identity. As with any Python pickle, do not rename or move the original class's module or qualified name without a compatibility alias.

deprecated_instance proxies over plain objects have no in-place-class requirement. They pickle the wrapped object itself.

docs.title: TypeError: <obj> is wrapped in a deprecation proxy and cannot be pickled directly
docs.text:
Versions before v0.11 raised this error. Since v0.11, pickle.dumps(proxy) reconstructs deprecated_instance proxies on unpickle with deprecation semantics preserved. Upgrade pyDeprecate if this error persists on such a proxy.

Q: I get TypeError: ... is wrapped in a deprecation proxy and cannot be pickled directly when passing a deprecated_instance proxy to pickle.dumps, multiprocessing, or joblib.

Two caveats remain:

  • The stream callable must be picklable by reference. Replace lambdas or closures with stream=None or stream=warnings.warn.
  • A deprecated_class alias itself commonly raises PicklingError when its proxy replaces the decorated class name. Use copy.deepcopy for class aliases. Instances of classes deprecated in place pickle successfully.

docs.title: My expiry gate reports more expired wrappers after upgrading
docs.text:
Since v0.11, validate_deprecation_expiry includes deprecated class members by default (include_members=True), matching find_deprecation_wrappers and generate_deprecation_table. Expired member wrappers — for example an __init__ carrying deprecation metadata — are counted, so totals can rise when you upgrade from before v0.11 even though your code is unchanged. The newly reported entries are real expired deprecations that were previously invisible to the gate.

Q: After upgrading pyDeprecate, validate_deprecation_expiry (and pydeprecate expiry) suddenly reports more expired wrappers than before — nothing in my code changed. Why?

from deprecate import validate_deprecation_expiry

# For testing purposes, we use the test module; normally you would import your own package
from tests.collections.api_deprecated import core as my_package

# Default scope includes deprecated class members
expired = validate_deprecation_expiry(my_package, "0.5")
print(f"Found {len(expired)} expired")

# Restore the previous module-level-only scope
expired = validate_deprecation_expiry(my_package, "0.5", include_members=False)
print(f"Found {len(expired)} expired")
Output: Found ... expired 
Found 31 expired
Found 28 expired

Prefer fixing the newly surfaced entries over passing include_members=False — the narrower scope hides genuinely expired member deprecations. Every audit function takes the same include_members switch, and every CLI subcommand takes --no-include-members (for example pydeprecate expiry src/mypackage --no-include-members).

docs.title: Why does pydeprecate all report policy violations but still exit 0?
docs.text:
No. all treats policy violations as advisory by default because its policy defaults encode one release convention rather than a universal rule.

Q: pydeprecate all src/mypackage prints a Deprecation Policy Violations table, but the command exits 0 and my CI step passes. Is the exit code wrong?

The defaults are min_grace="0.3" and message_required=True. Violations are printed for visibility but do not contribute to all's exit code unless you opt in.

Version Make policy violations fail all Since v0.16 Use pydeprecate all --gate=policy src/mypackage or gate = ["policy"] in [tool.pydeprecate]. Before v0.16 Add a separate policy step, as shown below.

The opt-in makes all exit 1 on policy violations from that same scan. Without it, these findings make all exit 1:

  • Invalid argument mappings make all exit 1.
  • Misconfigured targets make all exit 1.
  • Inner-order properties make all exit 1.
  • Deprecated-to-deprecated chains make all exit 1.
  • Expired wrappers make all exit 1.

Policy configuration errors are never advisory. An unreadable or unparsable nearest pyproject.toml, or malformed [tool.pydeprecate.policy] value, still exits 2 inside all. The message is Cannot read <path>: <err>. This failure is checked before the chains check runs.

Before v0.16, or to keep policy gating separate from all, give pydeprecate policy its own CI step.

Exit code Meaning 0 No violations. 1 Policy violations. 2 A malformed rule argument. 
# reports policy violations, but the exit code ignores them
pydeprecate all src/mypackage

# this is the step that fails the build
pydeprecate policy src/mypackage --min-grace=0.3 --message-required=True

Spell out the rule flags even when they match defaults. The command then records your project's promises. Future pyDeprecate default changes cannot silently change what CI enforces.

docs.title: How do I switch off a policy rule my project does not follow?
docs.text:
Both rules are independently controlled — pass None for min_grace or False for message_required. Nothing is all-or-nothing.

Q: My project removes deprecated code one minor after announcing it, so pydeprecate policy flags every wrapper with [min-grace]. I do not want to abandon the guidance rule to silence it.

Before disabling the window, consider retargeting it to your release cadence. min_grace is a version-shaped delta:

Value Required warning window "0.1" One minor. "0.3" (default) Three minors. "1.0" One major.

Choose your project's actual cadence to retain the gate. Disabling it leaves removal schedules unchecked. A 0.x project needs no special setting: a bump to 1.0 is a major step and clears any window.

Here is the difference between the two:

from deprecate import validate_deprecation_policy

# For testing purposes, we use the test module; normally you would import your own package
from tests.collections import policy as my_package

# Relax the window: one minor of warning is enough.
# The fixtures still trip it — one removes in the same release, one at a patch off any boundary.
violations = validate_deprecation_policy(my_package, recursive=False, min_grace="0.1")
print(f"Found {len(violations)} violations")

# Or drop the rule entirely and keep the guidance rule
violations = validate_deprecation_policy(my_package, recursive=False, min_grace=None)
print(f"Found {len(violations)} violations")
Output: f"Found {len(violations)} violations" 
Found 6 violations
Found 4 violations

The CLI exposes one flag per rule: --min-grace=0.1, --min-grace=None, and --message-required=False.

An unrecognized value is rejected before scanning with exit 2. The message names accepted spellings, so a typo cannot silently disable a rule.

docs.title: Where does pydeprecate policy take its rules from when I pass no flags?
docs.text:
Each rule resolves independently: command-line flag, then [tool.pydeprecate.policy] in pyproject.toml, then built-in default. The defaults are min-grace = "0.3" and message-required = true.

Q: I run a bare pydeprecate policy src/mypackage in CI and locally. Which rules apply, and can the project declare them once instead of every invocation repeating --min-grace and --message-required?

Declare your project's convention once:

[tool.pydeprecate.policy]
min-grace = "0.3"  # quoted — a TOML float 0.10 reads as 0.1; false switches the rule off
message-required = true

Configuration discovery follows the same search as --version auto-detection:

  1. Start at the scanned path's directory.
  2. Search up to two parents.
  3. Use the nearest table.

Bare module names never trigger this search. Running from an unrelated checkout therefore cannot adopt its policy.

Every run prints a Policy: header identifying each value's source: flag, pyproject.toml, or built-in.

Configuration failures and unknown keys:

  • Malformed values, unreadable files, and unparsable pyproject.toml files exit 2 with Cannot read <path>: <err>.
  • Unknown keys, such as min_grace with an underscore, are reported on stderr and ignored. They are never silently enforced.
  • On Python 3.9–3.10, the parser is tomli from the [audit] extra. Without it, a reachable pyproject.toml triggers an advisory instead of being skipped silently.

pydeprecate all uses these resolved settings for its advisory policy pass. Configuration-read failures still propagate as exit 2, checked before chains, even though violation counts are advisory.

The Python API does not read configuration files

validate_deprecation_policy() accepts a module object or importable name, never a filesystem path. Pass min_grace and message_required explicitly.

docs.title: How do I keep test fixtures or a legacy tree out of the audit?
docs.text:
Yes. Every scanning function and CLI subcommand accepts an exclude list of glob patterns matched against full dotted module names.

Q: My package ships my_package.tests (or a frozen my_package._legacy tree) with deliberately odd @deprecated wrappers. pydeprecate all reports them, and importing the fixtures is slow. Can the scan skip them?

For project configuration, use:

[tool.pydeprecate]
exclude = ["my_package.tests", "*._legacy*"]

You can also pass exclusions directly:

  • For the CLI, run pydeprecate all src/my_package --exclude='my_package.tests,*._legacy*'. Quote the value so the shell does not expand *.
  • In Python, call find_deprecation_wrappers(my_package, exclude=["my_package.tests"]).

A pattern matching a package excludes its whole subtree. The scan itself never imports excluded packages. A fixture raising at import time therefore neither slows the scan nor produces an audit: skipped warning.

Imports elsewhere still run. If other code in your package imports an excluded package, that import happens normally. Only the wrappers are filtered out.

The header Exclude: my_package.tests (pyproject.toml) identifies the exclusions and their source.

  • Use full names such as my_package.tests. Bare tests matches only a top-level module with that name.
  • A value other than a string or list of strings exits 2.

docs.title: UserWarning: audit: skipped <module> during a recursive scan
docs.text:
Recursive scans import every submodule and run its module-level code. If any submodule raises during import, the scanner warns and continues with the remaining modules. This includes exceptions beyond ImportError.

Q: A recursive audit scan (find_deprecation_wrappers, validate_deprecation_expiry, pydeprecate check / all) emits UserWarning: audit: skipped <module>: <exception>. What does it mean?

UserWarning: audit: skipped my_package.legacy_ext: RuntimeError('optional native extension not built')

Results cover every successfully imported module; only the named submodule is missing. Investigate and fix that submodule, or accept the gap if expected, such as for an optional dependency.

Skipped modules remain unaudited

A broken submodule no longer aborts the gate, but its deprecations remain unaudited until it imports cleanly.

The CLI also prints pydeprecate gap: module not audited: <module>: <exception> on stderr for each skipped submodule. This line appears even if your package's warnings filter hides the UserWarning.

docs.title: My pydeprecate pre-commit hook passes but misses deprecations
docs.text:
The remote hook (repo: https://github.com/Borda/pyDeprecate) runs in an isolated pre-commit environment. It contains pyDeprecate and its CLI dependencies, but lacks your package's runtime dependencies.

Q: I added the pydeprecate pre-commit hook and it always passes, but pydeprecate check in my virtual environment reports problems. Why?

The scan imports your package. Submodules with missing dependencies are skipped with UserWarning: audit: skipped <module>. Pre-commit hides output from passing hooks.

Choose a setup matching your audit needs:

  • Run a local hook (repo: local, language: system, entry: pydeprecate check) so the scan uses your development environment — the recommended setup for any package with runtime dependencies.

  • Use the remote hook with dependencies. List your package's dependencies in additional_dependencies. This replaces the hook's own list, so start with "pyDeprecate[audit]" and append yours.

  • For removal deadlines and policy rules only, use the import-free pydeprecate-expiry-static and pydeprecate-policy-static hooks, which need none of your dependencies (since v0.16).

Retain the hook's extras

Pip resolves the audit extra to the hook's own checkout. Without audit, missing packaging causes expiry and min-grace checks to warn and skip instead of failing. Without tomli on Python 3.9–3.10, [tool.pydeprecate] settings are ignored.

The audit guide contains the hook recipes.

docs.title: Can pydeprecate audit a package whose dependencies are not installed?
docs.text:
Yes, for removal deadlines and policy rules. Since v0.16.0, pydeprecate expiry --static and pydeprecate policy --static read source with ast without importing your package.

Q: Can pydeprecate audit a package whose dependencies are not installed?

The pydeprecate-expiry-static and pydeprecate-policy-static pre-commit hooks use the same approach. Neither runtime dependencies nor your package's import-time code run.

Recognized wrappers can be checked when the required settings are statically resolvable. Supported settings include literals, module-level names bound once to literals, and values splatted from a module-level dict literal.

Static coverage has limits

A recognized wrapper with unresolved settings prints pydeprecate gap: not statically resolvable: <file>:<line>: <reason>. This does not change the exit code unless strict mode is enabled. Read the gaps and spell settings literally where gating matters.

A loop or if block that calls deprecated prints an unrecognized use gap, and a computed globals() or setattr(sys.modules[...]) write leaves every wrapper of that module unresolved. These forms are invisible and produce no gap:

  • Wrappers built through getattr, importlib, or exec are invisible.
  • Wrappers imported from outside the scanned package are invisible.

check, chains, all, and status need imported wrappers and have no static mode. See Static mode. For reusable Python rows, see the Python static API.

docs.title: How do I audit deprecations without importing my package?
docs.text:
Call deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers_static(path) (since v0.16) to read source with ast without importing or executing the scanned package.

Pass its frozen StaticScanResult directly to validate_deprecation_expiry, validate_deprecation_policy, or generate_deprecation_table.

Inspect gaps and avoid stand-in targets. Always inspect .gaps for incomplete coverage, even when .wrappers is empty. Never call a row's stand-in target: it raises TypeError.

This suits missing dependencies, docs builds, and isolated audit scripts. Supply current_version to expiry when .version is None; otherwise expiry raises ImportError. The result shares the CLI --static blind spots: dynamic forms can remain invisible without a gap.

See the runnable Python example and limitations.

docs.title: My pydeprecate pre-commit hook fails: contains multiple packages
docs.text:
Without a path in args, the hook searches for a single package under src/, then at the repository root. A root containing multiple top-level packages, such as mypkg/ and tests/, is ambiguous. pyDeprecate stops with an error instead of scanning nothing and passing.

Q: The pydeprecate pre-commit hook fails with contains multiple packages (mypkg, tests) and a non-zero exit. What should I change?

Src-layout repositories and single-package roots resolve automatically. For multi-package repositories, name the package in the hook's args:

- id: pydeprecate-check
  args: [mypkg]

The same error, a usage error with exit 2, applies to every subcommand; see the audit guide.

docs.title: pydeprecate gap: other copy audited
docs.text:
The scan checked the copy named in the message, which may differ from the directory you passed. The Imported from: header identifies the file actually audited.

Q: The CLI prints pydeprecate gap: other copy audited: <pkg> was imported from <dir>, not from <scanned dir>. Were my deprecations checked?

Packages are imported by name. When the CLI process already has that name loaded, the scan uses the loaded copy.

This can happen when:

  • You scan a pyDeprecate fork or checkout while the CLI already uses its own deprecate package.
  • An editable install from another checkout resolves ahead of the requested directory on sys.path.

If the copies contain identical code, the result remains valid. For example, CI can install a wheel built from the checkout, then scan src/.

Otherwise, run the scan from the checkout's own virtual environment. Ensure the package name resolves to the directory you pass.

docs.title: Why does my CI step exit 3?
docs.text:
The audit did not run. Exit 3 represents a scan or internal error, rather than findings (exit 1) or a usage error (exit 2).

Q: pydeprecate check src/mypackage (or the GitHub Action) fails with exit code 3 and pydeprecate: scan error: … or pydeprecate: internal error: …. What does it mean?

Error Cause and action Scan error The scanned package's __init__ or named module raised during import, or its module-level code called sys.exit(). Install its runtime dependencies as for tests. Internal error A pyDeprecate bug occurred. The message names the exception and issue tracker for reporting it.

A failed submodule is a gap. A submodule import failure produces pydeprecate gap: module not audited. It preserves the exit code unless strict mode is enabled.

--exit-zero does not mask exit 3, and no --report-json file is written. Before v0.15, both error types exited 1, like findings.

docs.title: Why does pydeprecate check now fail on a wrapper it used to pass?
docs.text:
Since v0.15, misconfigured targets and inner-order properties are errors, as the CLI guide always promised. The scan exposes them through misconfigured_target and inner_order_property in find_deprecation_wrappers.

Q: After upgrading, pydeprecate check (and all) exits 1 with Found deprecated wrappers with a misconfigured target or Found inner-order @property @deprecated wrappers, on code that passed before.

Misconfiguration Effect Fix TargetMode.NOTIFY with args_mapping, attrs_mapping, or args_extra The mode ignores the mapping or extras. Old argument names are never migrated. Use TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP for argument renames, or drop the mapping for a plain notice. TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP without args_mapping There is nothing to remap. Supply a mapping or use a plain notice. target=False The target is invalid. Choose the appropriate supported target. @property above @deprecated Only the getter warns; setters and deleters added later stay silent. Put @deprecated(...) above @property.

docs.title: How do I accept one known expired wrapper without excluding its module?
docs.text:
Accept just that finding with --ignore='expired:mypackage.module:old_fn'. Alternatively, list the entry under ignore = [...] in [tool.pydeprecate] (since v0.16).

Q: pydeprecate expiry (or all) fails on a wrapper we deliberately keep one more release, and --exclude would hide every other wrapper of that module too.

Entry form Effect rule:module:symbol Accepts matching findings, with fnmatch globs in each part. module:symbol Accepts every rule for that symbol.

To accept a whole backlog:

  1. Write a report with --report-json.
  2. Pass that report to later runs with --baseline. Only newly added findings fail.

Suppressed findings do not fail the gate. Every run prints their count, and reports list them. They remain visible until fixed.

docs.title: How do I make the CI gate fail when part of the audit did not run?
docs.text:
Pass --strict (since v0.16), set strict = true under [tool.pydeprecate], or use fail-on-gap: true in the GitHub Action. Any recorded gap then makes the run exit 1, even without findings.

Q: pydeprecate all src/mypackage prints pydeprecate gap: module not audited: … or pydeprecate gap: version not resolved: … and still exits 0. How do I make such a run fail?

A strict run prints Strict mode: N gap(s) fail this run. after its gap lines. Without strict mode, gaps are advisory: they identify unaudited parts, while the exit code reflects completed checks.

Fix the cause named by the gap's hint. Usually this means installing a missing runtime dependency or passing a version with --version. Use --exclude for modules you never want audited.

Setting Effect Explicit --strict with --exit-zero Rejected with exit 2. --exit-zero alone or Action exit-zero: true Disables configured strict = true for that run. --no-strict Disables configured strict mode without --exit-zero.

Configured strict mode needs a TOML parser

Python 3.11+ includes one. On Python 3.9 and 3.10, install [audit] for tomli, or pass --strict explicitly.

Without a parser, configured strict = true is off. Only a stderr advisory is printed, and gaps do not fail the run.

docs.title: Why does the GitHub Action say the report is not of layout version 1?
docs.text:
The action runner only reads the report layout its own CLI writes: layout 1 since v0.15. A different layout usually means install: false selected another pyDeprecate version.

Q: The pyDeprecate GitHub Action warns the pyDeprecate report is not of layout version 1; ignoring it and adds no gap annotations or job summary, although the CLI ran.

The step still uses the CLI's exit code, so the gate result remains correct. Only annotations and the summary are skipped.

  • Pin the action to the installed release, such as uses: Borda/pyDeprecate@v0.16.0.
  • Alternatively, keep install: true so the action installs the CLI from its own ref.

docs.title: Why does a pyDeprecate annotation show no file or line?
docs.text:
The CLI cannot name a source location for every finding. Objects without a defining line include deprecated_instance data values, runtime-built classes, and code compiled from strings.

Q: The GitHub Action's annotation for a finding appears on the run summary instead of on a line of the pull request.

Static scans also cannot locate wrappers for objects defined in another module or bound more than once.

Since v0.16, a finding with a location uses the file and line of its wrapper's first decorator. A deprecated module is annotated on its file without a line.

Only checkout paths match pull requests

The repository root is the nearest directory holding .git at or above the job's working directory. Files outside it use absolute paths, which GitHub cannot match to the pull request. Scan the package in the checkout instead of an installed copy.

docs.title: Why did the GitHub Action skip my job summary?
docs.text:
The summary is optional and never changes the gate's exit code. It uses the table from --report-json, which the CLI writes only after a completed scan with exit 0 or 1.

Q: The action ran with summary: true, but the job summary is absent. It may warn that the gate wrote no pyDeprecate report, that no report is available, or show another summary warning.

A usage error (exit 2) or crashed scan (exit 3, such as a package import failure) produces neither a summary nor a summary warning. No scan finished; the step's error annotation names the exit code.

Runner warning Meaning and action "The gate wrote no pyDeprecate report" Report writing failed. Read the CLI's stderr immediately above the warning. "No pyDeprecate report is available" With install: false, an older pyDeprecate may lack --report-json. Keep install: true or upgrade the installed version. "No pyDeprecate report is available" after a temporary-directory warning The runner could not create its report directory. The preceding warning gives the OS error. "summary: true needs GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" The job is not on a GitHub runner. "could not write the job summary" The warning includes the OS error. "The gate's report holds no deprecation table" CLI table rendering failed. Its stderr explains why. "Could not read the pyDeprecate report" or "not of layout version" The report is corrupt or from another pyDeprecate version, for example through install: false. The preceding runner warning names the cause.

Report-reading and layout warnings do not change the gate result.

docs.title: My deprecated function raises DeprecatedError instead of warning
docs.text:
Something switched the deprecation to fatal. Check the wrapper, active exception scope, process-wide setting, and environment variable in that order.

Q: A call that used to emit a FutureWarning now raises deprecate.DeprecatedError. Nothing in my code changed.

  1. Read the wrapper's as_exception=True setting on its @deprecated, deprecated_class, deprecated_instance, or deprecated_module call.
  2. Look for an enclosing with deprecate.as_exceptions(): in the same thread or task.
  3. Check deprecate.AS_EXCEPTIONS. Application bootstrap code or a test fixture may set this process-wide attribute.
  4. Check DEPRECATE_AS_EXCEPTIONS. At import, values 1, true, yes, or on seed that attribute.

Fatal precedence is monotonic

A wrapper's as_exception=False cannot escape a True global. This prevents a wrapper flag from opting out of strict CI. Only the consumer's as_exceptions(False) scope or AS_EXCEPTIONS setting can override that global.

To find the source at the failing call site:

  1. Print deprecate.AS_EXCEPTIONS and os.environ.get("DEPRECATE_AS_EXCEPTIONS").
  2. Read get_deprecation_config(the_wrapper).as_exception for the wrapper's value.
  3. If all three read False, inspect the traceback's call stack for with as_exceptions(): or @as_exceptions().

An open as_exceptions() scope never appears in deprecate.AS_EXCEPTIONS.

docs.title: Why does as_exception ignore num_warns, and raise even with stream=None?
docs.text:
Both behaviors are intended. Fatal deprecations bypass num_warns and raise on every call, leaving warning counters untouched. stream=None silences messages but does not disable the fatal lifecycle state.

Q: I set num_warns=1 expecting one exception, or stream=None expecting silence, but every call to my fatal deprecation still raises.

The budget controls messages. If a fatal gate stopped after one call, a caller could retry inside except DeprecatedError and pass straight through.

Changing the stream affects presentation, so it cannot turn off a CI gate. skip_if does suppress fatal deprecations: while the wrapper is disabled, it is not a deprecation.

Fatal modules stop attribute-walking tools. A fatal deprecated_module raises on every public attribute access. This includes probes by pytest collection, Sphinx autodoc, pickle, and copy. These tools stop at the module instead of skipping it.

pyDeprecate's own audit remains unaffected. find_deprecation_wrappers() and the CLI read the module's __dict__ directly. Fatal modules are therefore still discovered and reported normally.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text:
Open a GitHub issue

If none of the above covers your situation, open an issue on GitHub Issues. Include the full traceback, the decorator call you used, and the Python and pyDeprecate versions (pip show pyDeprecate).

The same goes for a use case the library does not handle yet: describe what you are deprecating and what callers should see. We are happy to discuss it and integrate it when it fits.

docs.title: Coding Agent Recipes
docs.text: This page is for coding assistants that need to add a correct deprecation cycle to Python code.

docs.title: Install the coding-agent plugin
docs.text:
The repository contains a pydeprecate plugin with the same skills for Codex and Claude Code. It is available from the repository's default branch (early, pre-1.0). It is separate from the pyDeprecate library, and pip does not install agent skills.

Install from GitHub:

# Codex
codex plugin marketplace add Borda/pyDeprecate
codex plugin add pydeprecate@pydeprecate

# Claude Code
claude plugin marketplace add Borda/pyDeprecate
claude plugin install pydeprecate@pydeprecate

For local development or unpublished changes, run these commands from the repository root with . instead of Borda/pyDeprecate in the marketplace-add command. The plugin-install command stays the same.

The plugin provides $pydeprecate:sunset and $pydeprecate:prune in Codex, and /pydeprecate:sunset and /pydeprecate:prune in Claude Code.

Request Required inputs Example sunset implements a deprecation. It requires package or module scope plus deprecated_in and remove_in. “Sunset parse_config in acme.parsers, deprecated_in=1.4, remove_in=2.0.” prune removes compatibility. It requires scope plus the target release only. “Prune compatibility due by target release 2.0 from acme.parsers.”

Preview remains read-only. A removal plan requires an explicit release deadline: remove_in <= target release under PEP 440.

Release-candidate preparation

A plan also includes a remove_in whose base release equals an explicitly requested RC target (2.0rc1 for remove_in="2.0"). This applies only when the user is preparing that final release.

The plan keeps surviving functions or classes available for argument/attribute compatibility, and leaves incomplete scans unresolved. Use the consumer environment's existing pyDeprecate; expiry, policy and all audits need [audit]; the other audits do not.

The plugin source lives under plugins/pydeprecate/: .codex-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, skills/sunset/SKILL.md, and skills/prune/SKILL.md.

For adoption scans, ask:

“Scan src/acme for deprecation decorators, warnings, aliases, and shims; suggest supported pyDeprecate conversions without editing.”

The scan verifies installed or explicitly identified release support and returns convert, keep, or needs decision. It does not force dependencies or convert operational warnings. PEP 702 static-checker behavior is not equivalent merely because runtime metadata looks similar.

docs.title: Rules for agents
docs.text:
• Install package: pyDeprecate.
  • Import package: deprecate.
  • Prefer @deprecated(target=new_callable) for callable renames.
  • Prefer TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP for argument renames or removals.
  • Prefer deprecated_class for class renames.
  • Prefer deprecated_instance for object aliases.
  • Always include deprecated_in, remove_in, and a migration message when available.

docs.title: Function rename
docs.text:
from deprecate import deprecated


def detect_objects(value: int) -> int:
    return value + 1


@deprecated(target=detect_objects, deprecated_in="1.2", remove_in="2.0")
def detect(value: int) -> int:
    pass  # body never runs — pyDeprecate intercepts all calls before reaching here

docs.title: Argument rename
docs.text:
from deprecate import TargetMode, deprecated


@deprecated(
    target=TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP,
    args_mapping={"old": "new"},
    deprecated_in="1.2",
    remove_in="2.0",
)
def api(*, new: str) -> str:
    return new


print(api(old="demo"))
Output: api(old="demo") 
demo

docs.title: Anti-patterns
docs.text:
• Do not write import pydeprecate in Python code.
  • Do not use target=True for argument remapping.
  • Do not use target=None for warning-only behavior.
  • Do not call the replacement function manually inside the deprecated function body when pyDeprecate is already forwarding.

docs.title: Agent context files
docs.text:
• llms.txt
  • llms-full.txt

docs.title: Compare Python Deprecation Tools
docs.text: Python has several ways to signal deprecation. Choose based on whether you need warnings, static checker visibility, or runtime compatibility during an API migration.

docs.title: Quick comparison
docs.text:
This page holds the canonical comparison table.

Feature pyDeprecate warnings.warn deprecation Deprecated warnings.deprecated† Simple warnings ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Auto call forwarding ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ Generator / async ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ Argument mapping ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ Argument deprecation ✅ ✍️ ❌ via deprecated.params ❌ Class / Enum proxy ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ Docstring injection ✅ ❌ ✅ via deprecated.sphinx, deprecated.google or deprecated.numpy ❌ Version tracking ✅ ✍️ ✅ ✅ ❌ Prevent log spam ✅ ✍️ ❌ ✍️ ❌ Zero runtime deps ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ † Custom streams ✅ ✍️ ❌ ❌ ❌ CI audit tools ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ Testing helpers ✅ ❌ @fail_if_not_removed ❌ ❌ Static checker signal ✍️ ❌ ❌ ❌ ✅ Stacked argument remaps ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ Sphinx plugin ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ MkDocs plugin ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌
  • ✅ = supported, ❌ = not supported, ✍️ = possible but requires manual work. For pyDeprecate's static checker signal, stack @warnings.deprecated above @deprecated.
  • Plain warning decorators stack too: each deprecation.deprecated layer warns, then calls the next. The "Stacked argument remaps" row covers stacked layers that each remap arguments for one release, with unsupported combinations flagged by a decoration-time UserWarning.
  • The Deprecated cells were checked against the Deprecated 3.0.1 source. Its log-spam control is a warnings filter action such as "once".
  • † warnings.deprecated is in the standard library on Python 3.13+ (PEP 702) and available as the typing_extensions.deprecated backport on older versions.

docs.title: Roles and enforcement
docs.text:
Tool Documented role Migration and enforcement Docstring notices warnings.warn Emit one-off internal warnings. Write forwarding yourself; warning filters can escalate warnings to errors. Write notices yourself. warnings.deprecated Signal deprecation to static checkers, with optional runtime warnings, on Python 3.13+. PEP 702 does not provide forwarding, argument mapping, or CI audits. Not assessed here. deprecation Decorate functions with version-aware warnings. Emits UnsupportedWarning when current_version >= removed_in; @fail_if_not_removed fails tests that catch it. Appends deprecation details. Deprecated Decorate functions, classes, or methods with warnings. action="error" escalates warnings; this is not version-driven enforcement. Yes, via deprecated.sphinx, or Google and NumPy docstring sections via deprecated.google and deprecated.numpy. pyDeprecate (this library) Keep callers compatible during API migrations. Forward calls, remap arguments, proxy classes/objects, test warnings, and audit deadlines in CI. Optional Sphinx or MkDocs notices with update_docstring=True.

Comparison scope

Unverified feature verdicts are omitted. This is a positioning guide, not a complete audit of every tool's features. Report inaccuracies.

A warning is not an exception

deprecation.UnsupportedWarning is a DeprecationWarning subclass. It becomes an exception only when warning filters escalate it.

The version comparison happens at decoration time. See the implementation.

docs.title: Use warnings.warn when
docs.text:
Use raw warnings for small internal messages where callers do not need a compatibility shim.

import warnings


def internal_hook() -> None:
    warnings.warn("internal_hook is deprecated", DeprecationWarning, stacklevel=2)


internal_hook()  # warns: DeprecationWarning
print("Hook completed")
Output: internal_hook() 
Hook completed

docs.title: Use warnings.deprecated when
docs.text:
Use PEP 702 for static checker visibility when runtime behavior does not need to change.

from typing_extensions import deprecated
from tests.collections.api_current import core as current

# NEW API — compute a sum with the current implementation.
compute_sum = current.base_sum_kwargs


# DEPRECATED API — mark the previous addition entry point for static checkers.
@deprecated("Use compute_sum instead.", category=None)
def addition(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return compute_sum(a, b)


print(addition(1, 2))
Output: addition(1, 2) 
3

Python versions and runtime cost

warnings.deprecated is in the standard library on Python 3.13+. Use the typing_extensions.deprecated backport on earlier versions. With category=None, the decorator returns the original object, adding no per-call wrapper overhead.

Suppressing the warning through a filter does not remove that wrapper. See PEP 702.

docs.title: Use pyDeprecate when
docs.text:
Use pyDeprecate when old callers must keep working while receiving a deprecation warning.

from deprecate import deprecated
from tests.collections.api_current import core as current
from tests.collections.api_deprecated import core

# NEW API — compute a sum with the current implementation.
compute_sum = current.base_sum_kwargs

# DEPRECATED API — addition forwards to compute_sum.
addition = deprecated(target=compute_sum, deprecated_in="1.2", remove_in="2.0")(core.original_sum)
print(addition(1, 2))  # warns: FutureWarning
Output: addition(1, 2) 
3

Decorator and assignment forms

These examples wrap imported collection functions to keep them executable. In your library, apply the same configuration as @deprecated(...) above the deprecated definition. Forwarding bypasses the source body.

docs.title: Migrating from warnings.warn
docs.text: Replace manual forwarding boilerplate with a single decorator.

docs.title: Before
docs.text:
import warnings
from tests.collections.api_current import core as current

# NEW API — compute a sum with the current implementation.
compute_sum = current.base_sum_kwargs


# DEPRECATED API — addition warns and forwards manually.
def addition(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    warnings.warn("addition is deprecated; use compute_sum instead.", DeprecationWarning, stacklevel=2)
    return compute_sum(a, b)


print(addition(1, 2))  # warns: DeprecationWarning
Output: addition(1, 2) 
3

docs.title: After
docs.text:
from deprecate import deprecated
from tests.collections.api_current import core as current
from tests.collections.api_deprecated import core

# NEW API — compute a sum with the current implementation.
compute_sum = current.base_sum_kwargs

# DEPRECATED API — addition forwards without manual warning code.
addition = deprecated(target=compute_sum, deprecated_in="1.2", remove_in="2.0")(core.original_sum)
print(addition(1, 2))  # warns: FutureWarning
Output: addition(1, 2) 
3

docs.title: Migrating from deprecation
docs.text: Replace the version-aware decorator and manual forwarding with a pyDeprecate target.

docs.title: Before
docs.text:
# phmdoctest:skip — shows the third-party API being migrated from
import deprecation
from tests.collections.api_current import core as current

# NEW API — compute a sum with the current implementation.
compute_sum = current.base_sum_kwargs


# DEPRECATED API — addition warns, then forwards manually.
@deprecation.deprecated(
    deprecated_in="1.2", removed_in="2.0", current_version="1.2", details="Use compute_sum instead."
)
def addition(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """Add two values through the previous entry point."""
    return compute_sum(a, b)


print(addition(1, 2))  # warns: DeprecationWarning
Output: addition(1, 2) 
3

docs.title: After
docs.text:
from deprecate import deprecated
from tests.collections.api_current import core as current
from tests.collections.api_deprecated import core

# NEW API — compute a sum with the current implementation.
compute_sum = current.base_sum_kwargs

# DEPRECATED API — addition delegates forwarding to pyDeprecate.
addition = deprecated(target=compute_sum, deprecated_in="1.2", remove_in="2.0")(core.original_sum)
print(addition(1, 2))  # warns: FutureWarning
Output: addition(1, 2) 
3

Migration differences

Rename removed_in to remove_in. pyDeprecate defaults to FutureWarning. It does not use current_version to switch warning classes.

Use fatal mode or CI expiry checks for enforcement. Enable update_docstring=True if you need injected notices.

docs.title: Migrating from Deprecated
docs.text: Replace the Deprecated warning decorator and manual forwarding with a pyDeprecate target.

docs.title: Before
docs.text:
# phmdoctest:skip — shows the third-party API being migrated from
from deprecated import deprecated
from tests.collections.api_current import core as current

# NEW API — compute a sum with the current implementation.
compute_sum = current.base_sum_kwargs


# DEPRECATED API — addition warns, then forwards manually.
@deprecated(version="1.2", reason="Use compute_sum instead.")
def addition(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return compute_sum(a, b)


print(addition(1, 2))  # warns: DeprecationWarning
Output: addition(1, 2) 
3

docs.title: After
docs.text:
from deprecate import deprecated
from tests.collections.api_current import core as current
from tests.collections.api_deprecated import core

# NEW API — compute a sum with the current implementation.
compute_sum = current.base_sum_kwargs

# DEPRECATED API — addition delegates forwarding to pyDeprecate.
addition = deprecated(target=compute_sum, deprecated_in="1.2", remove_in="2.0")(core.original_sum)
print(addition(1, 2))  # warns: FutureWarning
Output: addition(1, 2) 
3

Configuration changes

Translate version to deprecated_in and supply a remove_in deadline. The target supplies the replacement guidance in the warning. pyDeprecate defaults to FutureWarning.

Replace action="error" with as_exception=True when calls must fail. This raises DeprecatedError instead of a warning exception.

docs.title: Turning the warning into an error at a chosen version
docs.text:
Compute as_exception from your package version to choose when deprecated calls must fail.

from deprecate import DeprecatedError, TargetMode, deprecated_callable
from tests.collections.api_current import core as current

PACKAGE_VERSION = (1, 3)  # In a real package, parse your own __version__.
ERROR_IN = (1, 3)  # Callers must stop using the previous name in this release.

# NEW API — increment a value with the current implementation.
increment_value = current.increment_value

# DEPRECATED API — the previous entry point becomes fatal at ERROR_IN.
increment = deprecated_callable(TargetMode.NOTIFY, "1.0", "2.0", as_exception=PACKAGE_VERSION >= ERROR_IN)(
    increment_value
)

try:
    increment(1)
except DeprecatedError as err:
    print(err)
Output: increment(1) 
The `increment_value` was deprecated since v1.0. It will be removed in v2.0.

With plain warnings.warn, add an explicit raise or configure warning filters to escalate it. pyDeprecate's as_exception=True raises DeprecatedError before executing the source or target.

As a release-time backstop, pydeprecate expiry in CI exits 1 when a wrapper is past its remove_in deadline. See Fatal deprecations for the full behaviour.

docs.title: Helping callers migrate
docs.text:
Make deprecated usage fail in callers' CI so they can replace affected calls before removal.

  1. Run the test suite with the relevant warning category promoted to an error.

    python -W error::FutureWarning -m pytest
python -W error::DeprecationWarning -m pytest

  2. Keep the policy in pytest.ini when it should apply to every pytest run.

    [pytest]
filterwarnings =
    error::FutureWarning

  3. Replace each reported call using its warning's migration message, then rerun the suite.

Warning categories and coverage

pyDeprecate uses FutureWarning by default. Use error::DeprecationWarning for tools emitting that category. These filters affect Python warnings, not custom logging streams or silent wrappers.

Only executed paths can reveal deprecated calls. See Python warning filters and pytest warning configuration.

docs.title: Other tools
docs.text:
• debtcollector provides deprecation patterns, including removals, moves, and renames.
  • deprecated-params wraps functions, classes, and methods to deprecate keyword parameters.
  • wrapt is a dependency of Deprecated. It is not a peer deprecation tool in this comparison.
  • pytest.deprecated_call checks for DeprecationWarning, PendingDeprecationWarning, or FutureWarning. It is a test helper, not a deprecation decorator.

Unverified capabilities

Version-driven removal enforcement for debtcollector was not verified. No verdict is assigned here. Only the documented keyword-parameter purpose of deprecated-params is compared.

docs.title: Testing a migrated caller
docs.text:
Use deprecate.assert_no_warnings to check that a migrated call no longer warns; pytest.deprecated_call checks the opposite expectation.

from deprecate import assert_no_warnings
from tests.collections.api_current import core as current

# NEW API — callers use the replacement directly after migration.
compute_sum = current.base_sum_kwargs
with assert_no_warnings(FutureWarning):
    result = compute_sum(1, 2)
print(result)
Output: result 
3

docs.title: Decision guide
docs.text:
• Use warnings.warn when you only need an internal warning without forwarding or CI audits.
  • Use warnings.deprecated on Python 3.13+ when you only need static checker visibility.
  • Use pyDeprecate when public callers need runtime compatibility.
  • Use pyDeprecate for async def functions, generator functions, or async generators.
  • Use TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP for argument renames or dropped argument compatibility.
  • Use deprecated_class or deprecated_instance for class, constant, or object alias compatibility.
  • Use pyDeprecate audit tools for removal deadline checks in CI.

docs.title: Fair strengths in alternative tools worth considering
docs.text:
• warnings.deprecated provides native static diagnostics in mypy, pyright, and IDEs. With category=None, it adds no per-call wrapper overhead.
  • deprecation includes @fail_if_not_removed for test-failure enforcement when removal deadlines are reached.
  • Deprecated offers deprecated.sphinx.versionadded and deprecated.sphinx.versionchanged to inject Sphinx lifecycle directives into docstrings. Its deprecated.params decorator deprecates individual parameters.
  • warnings.warn needs no dependency and has a small surface for internal notices.

docs.text:

docs.title: Audit Tools
docs.text:
See policy enforcement, CI integration, and testing deprecated code for the companion guides.

Audit tools catch four common problems before they reach users:

Problem Detection API Example Zombie code. validate_deprecation_expiry() A remove_in deadline passes without code removal. Chained deprecations. validate_deprecation_chains() A wrapper targets another deprecated function and emits two notices. Misconfigured wrappers. find_deprecation_wrappers() An args_mapping key has a typo and silently does nothing. Policy violations. validate_deprecation_policy() Removal follows announcement by one patch, or the warning names no replacement. Version changes: v0.6, v0.8, v0.13

Renamed in v0.6. find_deprecated_callables is now find_deprecation_wrappers, validate_deprecated_callable is now validate_deprecation_wrapper, and DeprecatedCallableInfo is now DeprecationWrapperInfo. The old names remain exported for backwards compatibility but will be removed in v1.0.

Breaking change in v0.8: __deprecated__.target type changed. In v0.8, DeprecationConfig.target now always stores a TargetMode enum member or a Callable — never a raw boolean sentinel. Code inspecting this attribute must be updated:

The direct metadata reads below apply only through v0.12; v0.13 code must use get_deprecation_config(func) as shown in the next section.

Before v0.8 v0.8-v0.12 func.__deprecated__.target is None func.__deprecated__.target is TargetMode.NOTIFY func.__deprecated__.target is True func.__deprecated__.target is TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP func.__deprecated__.target is False func.__deprecated__.misconfigured

Breaking change in v0.13: __deprecated__ is now a plain message string. Since v0.13, __deprecated__ holds a PEP 702-conformant message string instead of the DeprecationConfig object. PEP-702-aware tooling, including IDE hover, pyright, and mypy, can read this string correctly.

The config object moved to __deprecation_config__. Read it through the public get_deprecation_config(obj) helper rather than either attribute directly:

Before v0.13 v0.13+ func.__deprecated__.target get_deprecation_config(func).target func.__deprecated__.deprecated_in get_deprecation_config(func).deprecated_in isinstance(func.__deprecated__, DeprecationConfig) get_deprecation_config(func) is not None

Every wrapper kind is affected — functions, methods, class proxies, instance proxies, and modules. See the v0.12-to-v0.13 migration guide for the full list.

docs.title: Scanning from Python without importing
docs.text:
Use deprecate.audit.find_deprecation_wrappers_static() (since v0.16) for source-only discovery through ast, without importing or executing the scanned package.

This helps when:

  • Dependencies are missing from the audit environment.
  • A docs build must not execute package initialization.
  • An isolated script needs source-only discovery.

Pass a package directory, a Python module file, a plain directory, or a top-level module name.

Dotted module names are refused because locating them would import their parents. Package submodules are read recursively by default. Plain directories include only top-level Python files.

Set recursive, include_members, and module-name exclude globs on the scan itself.

The frozen StaticScanResult stores the scan results:

Field Value .wrappers A tuple of rows. .gaps Ordered "<kind>: <detail>" strings. .version A version resolved without imports, or None.

Pass this result directly to expiry, policy, and table APIs to reuse rows without another scan.

This example runs from the repository root against the real static collection:

from deprecate.audit import (
    find_deprecation_wrappers_static,
    generate_deprecation_table,
    validate_deprecation_expiry,
    validate_deprecation_policy,
)

scan = find_deprecation_wrappers_static("tests/collections/static_forms.py")
print("Wrappers:", len(scan.wrappers))
for gap in scan.gaps:
    print(gap)

expired = validate_deprecation_expiry(scan, current_version="2.0")
violations = validate_deprecation_policy(scan)
report = generate_deprecation_table(scan, current_version="2.0")
print("Expired:", len(expired))
print("Policy violations:", len(violations))
# Show the table header and one source-derived row.
print(report.splitlines()[1])
print(next(line for line in report.splitlines() if "static_forms.forward_sum`" in line))

| Original API | API Type | New API | Deprecated | Remove | Current Status |

Consuming a completed scan. Install pyDeprecate[audit] for version comparisons. Expiry and table generation default to scan.version.

Supply current_version explicitly when that version is unavailable. Otherwise, expiry raises ImportError, while the table shows unknown status.

Policy checks only settings resolved for each rule. It never reads pyproject.toml policy settings.

Leave consumer recursive and include_members at their defaults. Passing False with a completed result raises ValueError.

Source rows are approximations

Always read .gaps, even when .wrappers or validator results are empty. A gap marks incomplete coverage. Some dynamic forms are invisible without a gap.

Row targets are stand-ins. Calling row.deprecated_info.target() when it is a synthetic target raises TypeError.

Use an import-mode audit with the package dependencies available for full runtime discovery.

The API shares the CLI --static source reader and its blind spots.

The Python API also accepts module files and renders tables from results. CLI status has no --static mode.

docs.title: Validating Wrapper Configuration
docs.text:
Validate wrappers to check argument names, mapping effects, and targets:

  • args_mapping keys must exist in the function signature.
  • The mapping must have a real effect.
  • The target must not point back to the same function.

validate_deprecation_wrapper() inspects one decorated callable, a proxy, or a module deprecated with deprecated_module(). find_deprecation_wrappers() scans an entire package.

Both functions return DeprecationWrapperInfo dataclasses.

Field Meaning module The defining module name, empty for direct validation. function The function name. deprecated_info The decorator's __deprecation_config__ attribute, a DeprecationConfig dataclass. invalid_args args_mapping keys absent from the function signature. empty_args_mapping True when args_mapping is None or empty. identity_args_mapping Arguments whose key equals their value, such as {"arg": "arg"}, with no effect. self_reference True when the target points to the same function. no_effect True for zero-impact wrappers: self-reference, empty mapping, or all-identity mapping. misconfigured_target True when the target contradicts its configuration; see the cases below. all_identity True when every args_mapping entry maps a key to itself. chain_type The chain classification, such as TARGET or STACKED. empty_deprecated_in True when deprecated_in is absent or empty; useful for CI version-annotation checks. api_type The inferred report kind: for example, callable, args, class, dataclass attributes, or class method. pep702_message None on pyDeprecate rows; the decorator's message string, possibly empty, on PEP 702-only rows. args_mapping_auto_expanded args_mapping keys copied automatically from attrs_mapping by the dataclass dual-surface expansion; empty otherwise. args_mapping_positional_only args_mapping old keys whose target is a positional-only constructor parameter; empty otherwise. inner_order_property True for the inner-order @property @deprecated shape, where only the getter warns; check fails on it. source_file, source_line Since v0.16, the absolute source file and definition line; see the exceptions below.

Contradictory targets. misconfigured_target covers these cases:

  • NOTIFY has an args_mapping, args_extra, or attrs_mapping.
  • ARGS_REMAP has an empty args_mapping, or an attrs_mapping next to its args_mapping.
  • deprecated_class(target=TargetMode.ATTRS_REMAP) has no attrs_mapping, or has an args_mapping or args_extra.
  • A served object is not callable but has an args_mapping or args_extra.
  • The target is the invalid target=False.

Read this audit field in CI rather than DeprecationConfig.misconfigured. They are not identical: legacy target=True skips callable-mode validation, leaving DeprecationConfig.misconfigured=False. The audit still flags an ARGS_REMAP wrapper with an empty mapping.

PEP 702 rows and representations. find_deprecation_wrappers(..., include_pep702=True) also reports symbols deprecated only with warnings.deprecated. Their rows have no versions, so empty_deprecated_in is True. See PEP 702-only deprecations.

api_type is excluded from repr() to keep snapshot tests stable. pep702_message is also excluded from repr().

Source locations. source_line points to the first, outermost decorator, including a functools.lru_cache above @deprecated. A class may point to its class line or its decorator. Functions point to their outermost @ line.

Both source fields are None for these objects:

  • A deprecated_instance data object.
  • A runtime-built class, such as a functional Enum or a type() call.
  • A function compiled from a string.

On Python 3.13+, an exec-built class may be attributed to a real module's file when its namespace names that module. A deprecated module has its file but no line. Neither field participates in equality or repr(), preserving existing comparisons.

Cache fields leave in v1.0

deprecated_info is a DeprecationConfig. These audit metadata fields are stable:

Fields Role deprecated_in, remove_in, name, target They describe the deprecation. args_mapping, args_extra, attrs_mapping They describe forwarding and renaming. misconfigured, docstring_style, message_template, as_exception They describe configuration and messaging. args_mapping_auto_expanded, args_mapping_positional_only, call_options_inert They describe mapping and call-option audit metadata.

Eight internal call-time cache fields avoid repeated signature inspection:

Fields Role target_positional_only, target_positional_only_order They cache target positional-only parameters. source_positional_only, source_positional_only_order, source_var_positional_prefix They cache source positional information. target_all_param_names, target_accepts_var_positional, target_accepts_var_keyword They cache accepted target parameters.

These eight fields will leave DeprecationConfig in v1.0. Do not read them in audit or CI code.

docs.title: Validating a single function
docs.text:
validate_deprecation_wrapper() extracts the configuration from the function's __deprecation_config__ attribute and returns a DeprecationWrapperInfo dataclass. Use it in development or in a targeted pytest assertion to confirm a specific wrapper is sound before shipping.

from deprecate import TargetMode, validate_deprecation_wrapper, deprecated, DeprecationWrapperInfo


# Define your deprecated function
@deprecated(target=TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP, args_mapping={"old_arg": "new_arg"}, deprecated_in="1.0")
def my_func(old_arg: int = 0, new_arg: int = 0) -> int:
    return new_arg


# Validate the configuration - automatically extracts `args_mapping` and target from the decorator
result = validate_deprecation_wrapper(my_func)


# DeprecationWrapperInfo(
#   function='my_func',
#   invalid_args=[],
#   empty_args_mapping=False,
#   identity_args_mapping=[],
#   self_reference=False,
#   no_effect=False
# )


# Example: Function with invalid args_mapping
@deprecated(target=TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP, args_mapping={"nonexistent": "new_arg"}, deprecated_in="1.0")
def bad_func(real_arg: int = 0) -> int:
    return real_arg


result = validate_deprecation_wrapper(bad_func)
# result.invalid_args == ['nonexistent']
print(result)


# Example: Function with empty mapping (no effect)
@deprecated(target=TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP, args_mapping={}, deprecated_in="1.0")
def empty_func(arg: int = 0) -> int:
    return arg


result = validate_deprecation_wrapper(empty_func)
# result.empty_args_mapping == True, result.no_effect == True
print(result)

# Quick check if wrapper has any effect
if result.no_effect:
    print("Warning: This wrapper configuration has zero impact!")
Output: "Warning: This wrapper configuration has zero impact!" 
DeprecationWrapperInfo(module='', function='bad_func', deprecated_info=DeprecationConfig(deprecated_in='1.0', remove_in='', name='bad_func', target=<TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP: 'args_remap'>, args_mapping={'nonexistent': 'new_arg'}, args_extra=None, misconfigured=False, docstring_style='rst', message_template=None, attrs_mapping=None, as_exception=None, args_mapping_auto_expanded=(), args_mapping_positional_only=(), target_positional_only=frozenset(), source_positional_only=frozenset(), source_var_positional_prefix=0, call_options_inert=False), invalid_args=['nonexistent'], empty_args_mapping=False, identity_args_mapping=[], self_reference=False, no_effect=False, misconfigured_target=False, all_identity=False, chain_type=None, empty_deprecated_in=False, args_mapping_auto_expanded=[], args_mapping_positional_only=[], inner_order_property=False)
DeprecationWrapperInfo(module='', function='empty_func', deprecated_info=DeprecationConfig(deprecated_in='1.0', remove_in='', name='empty_func', target=<TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP: 'args_remap'>, args_mapping={}, args_extra=None, misconfigured=True, docstring_style='rst', message_template=None, attrs_mapping=None, as_exception=None, args_mapping_auto_expanded=(), args_mapping_positional_only=(), target_positional_only=frozenset(), source_positional_only=frozenset(), source_var_positional_prefix=0, call_options_inert=False), invalid_args=[], empty_args_mapping=True, identity_args_mapping=[], self_reference=False, no_effect=True, misconfigured_target=True, all_identity=False, chain_type=None, empty_deprecated_in=False, args_mapping_auto_expanded=[], args_mapping_positional_only=[], inner_order_property=False)
