docs.title: Attributes
docs.text: Use selective attribute deprecation when only particular names need migration; see Classes for whole-class deprecation.

docs.title: Selective attribute deprecation
docs.text:
Use attrs_mapping on deprecated_class() to deprecate selected attribute names while leaving all others silent. It covers renames, spelling corrections such as color → colour, and individual warn-only notices.

Mapping keys are deprecated attribute names:

Value Behavior A canonical name string Reads, writes, and deletes warn and redirect against the active class. None Access warns without renaming the attribute.

Unlisted attributes stay silent.

Mapping validation

Non-None values must exist on the target class when supplied, or otherwise on the wrapped source class. Redirect chains such as {"a": "b", "b": "c"} are accepted and audited as ChainType.STACKED. Cycles such as {"a": "b", "b": "a"} raise immediately.

docs.title: Decorator syntax — attribute rename
docs.text:
Apply @deprecated_class(attrs_mapping=...) at class definition time. Only the attribute names listed as keys emit a FutureWarning; all others pass through silently:

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — Palette.colour is the canonical spelling
# DEPRECATED API — Palette.color redirects to Palette.colour
@deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"color": "colour"},  # "color" is the deprecated spelling
    deprecated_in="2.0",
    remove_in="3.0",
)
# NEW API — the canonical colour attribute
class Palette:
    colour: str = "red"  # canonical name
    size: int = 10  # unlisted — silent passthrough, no warning


# Deprecated alias — warns: "The `color` was deprecated since v2.0 in favor of `Palette.colour`."
print(Palette.color)  # red

# Canonical names — silent passthrough, no warning
print(Palette.colour)  # red
print(Palette.size)  # 10
Output: Palette.color; Palette.colour; Palette.size 
red
red
10

The wrapper form is equivalent to decorator syntax. Use it for existing classes or to apply deprecation outside the class definition:

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — canonical configuration attributes
class Config:
    colour: str = "red"
    size: int = 42
    timeout: int = 30


# DEPRECATED API — "color" redirects to "colour"; "size" warns without renaming
DeprecatedConfig = deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"color": "colour", "size": None},
    deprecated_in="1.0",
    remove_in="2.0",
)(Config)

print(DeprecatedConfig.color)  # warns → returns Config.colour ("red")
print(DeprecatedConfig.colour)  # silent passthrough ("red")
print(DeprecatedConfig.size)  # warns (warn-only, size=42 unchanged)
Output: DeprecatedConfig.color; DeprecatedConfig.colour; DeprecatedConfig.size 
red
red
42

docs.title: Reads, writes, and deletes all redirect
docs.text:
The attrs_mapping interception applies to all three access modes. Writing to a deprecated attribute alias warns and sets the canonical attribute instead:

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — the canonical colour attribute
class Palette:
    colour: str = "red"


# DEPRECATED API — the color spelling redirects to colour
DeprecatedPalette = deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"color": "colour"},  # "color" is the deprecated spelling
    deprecated_in="1.0",
    remove_in="2.0",
)(Palette)

# Write — warns: FutureWarning and redirects to Palette.colour
DeprecatedPalette.color = "blue"  # warns: FutureWarning

# Canonical attribute now holds the new value (no warning on canonical reads)
print(Palette.colour)  # blue
Output: Palette.colour 
blue

docs.title: Warn-only with None redirect
docs.text:
Map a deprecated attribute to None to emit a warning on access without renaming anything. The attribute is fetched by its original name on the active class after the warning fires. Use this when an attribute is going away with no replacement:

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — callers should stop using the size attribute
class Widget:
    size: int = 42  # scheduled for removal — callers should stop reading it


# DEPRECATED API — size warns without a replacement
DeprecatedWidget = deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"size": None},  # warn-only, no rename
    deprecated_in="1.0",
    remove_in="2.0",
)(Widget)

# Warns: "The `size` was deprecated since v1.0. It will be removed in v2.0."
print(DeprecatedWidget.size)  # 42 — value still returned, just warned

# Second access is silent — num_warns=1 budget exhausted
print(DeprecatedWidget.size)  # 42 — no second warning
Output: DeprecatedWidget.size; DeprecatedWidget.size (second call) 
42
42

docs.title: Per-attribute independent warning budgets
docs.text:
Each deprecated attribute name has an independent warning counter. With num_warns=1, the default, two different deprecated aliases each warn once. This produces two warnings rather than sharing one budget:

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — canonical configuration attributes
class Config:
    colour: str = "red"
    text: str = "hello"


# DEPRECATED API — color and txt keep independent warning budgets
proxy = deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"color": "colour", "txt": "text"},
    deprecated_in="1.0",
    remove_in="2.0",
)(Config)

print(proxy.color)  # warns: FutureWarning — "color" budget consumed
print(proxy.txt)  # warns: FutureWarning — "txt" budget consumed (independent counter)

# Both budgets now exhausted — subsequent accesses are silent
print(proxy.color)  # silent
print(proxy.txt)  # silent
Output: proxy.color; proxy.txt; proxy.color (silent); proxy.txt (silent) 
red
hello
red
hello

docs.title: Enum — deprecated member aliases
docs.text:
attrs_mapping also works on Enum proxies. Use it when member names change, such as a casing migration. Wrap the canonical Enum and register deprecated names as aliases:

from enum import Enum
from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — canonical uppercase direction names
class Direction(Enum):
    NORTH = "N"
    SOUTH = "S"
    EAST = "E"
    WEST = "W"


# DEPRECATED API — lowercase aliases redirect to canonical uppercase members
LegacyDirection = deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"north": "NORTH", "south": "SOUTH"},
    deprecated_in="1.0",
    remove_in="2.0",
)(Direction)

# Deprecated lowercase alias — warns and returns the canonical Direction.NORTH member
print(LegacyDirection.north is Direction.NORTH)  # True

# Canonical uppercase name — silent passthrough, no warning
print(LegacyDirection.NORTH is Direction.NORTH)  # True
Output: LegacyDirection.north is Direction.NORTH; LegacyDirection.NORTH is Direction.NORTH 
True
True

attrs_mapping can be combined with target=NewClass; listed attribute aliases redirect to their canonical counterparts on the target class. Unlisted attributes and calls continue to use the normal target-forwarding behaviour.

Audit visibility

find_deprecation_wrappers discovers the proxy via its class-level __deprecation_config__. Individual attrs_mapping entries are data inside the single proxy config and are not emitted as separate DeprecationWrapperInfo records. All entries share the same deprecated_in/remove_in lifecycle.

docs.title: Explicit TargetMode.ATTRS_REMAP form
docs.text:
Passing attrs_mapping alone auto-resolves to TargetMode.ATTRS_REMAP. Explicitly passing target=TargetMode.ATTRS_REMAP with attrs_mapping has identical behavior. The explicit form makes intent visible at the call site:

from deprecate import TargetMode, deprecated_class


# NEW API — the canonical colour attribute
class Palette:
    colour: str = "red"  # canonical name


# Explicit form — equivalent to passing `attrs_mapping` alone
# DEPRECATED API — the color spelling redirects to colour
DeprecatedPalette = deprecated_class(
    target=TargetMode.ATTRS_REMAP,
    attrs_mapping={"color": "colour"},
    deprecated_in="1.0",
    remove_in="2.0",
)(Palette)

print(DeprecatedPalette.color)  # warns → returns "red"
Output: DeprecatedPalette.color 
red

Decoration-time validation

These misconfigurations emit UserWarning at decoration time, planned to become TypeError in v1.0:

Misconfiguration Why it is wrong target=TargetMode.ATTRS_REMAP without attrs_mapping ATTRS_REMAP requires deprecated attribute names in attrs_mapping. Without them, the proxy has no selective effect. attrs_mapping={} An empty mapping has no effect. Remove it or add deprecated attribute names. target=TargetMode.NOTIFY with attrs_mapping NOTIFY means warn-only without redirection. The proxy keeps NOTIFY; the mapping remains inert but preserved in audit metadata and flagged misconfigured. Omit target to auto-resolve to ATTRS_REMAP.

Explicit modes stay explicit. Explicit configuration is never silently rewritten; auto-resolution fills in only an omitted target. For blanket per-access warnings plus selective attribute renaming, stack two deprecated_class() layers. See Nested proxy wrappers.

Proxy-only mode. TargetMode.ATTRS_REMAP works only with proxies. @deprecated(target=TargetMode.ATTRS_REMAP) raises TypeError at decoration time for every source: functions, methods, properties, and classes. The front door cannot expose attrs_mapping, so this mode could never redirect anything there. The error points to deprecated_class(attrs_mapping=...), or deprecated_instance(obj, attrs_mapping=...) for objects.

docs.title: Callable target with attribute redirection
docs.text:
Combine target=NewClass and attrs_mapping for full class replacement with renamed attributes:

  • Listed deprecated aliases resolve against NewClass.
  • Unlisted attributes and instantiation calls also forward to NewClass.
  • None entries keep their original names. For example, attrs_mapping={"size": None} warns before reading, writing, or deleting NewClass.size.
from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — Config uses the shorter lr name
class Config:
    lr: float = 0.01  # canonical name in the new class
    batch_size: int = 32  # unchanged attribute


# DEPRECATED API — learning_rate redirects to Config.lr
@deprecated_class(
    target=Config,
    attrs_mapping={"learning_rate": "lr"},  # "learning_rate" was renamed to "lr"
    deprecated_in="2.0",
    remove_in="3.0",
    num_warns=-1,
)
class LegacyConfig:
    learning_rate: float = 0.01  # old name — will warn
    lr: float = 0.01  # canonical alias also present


print(LegacyConfig.learning_rate)  # warns: FutureWarning — value from Config.lr

print(LegacyConfig.lr)  # silent — canonical name

print(LegacyConfig.batch_size)  # silent — unlisted attribute
Output: LegacyConfig.learning_rate; LegacyConfig.lr; LegacyConfig.batch_size 
0.01
0.01
32

Instantiation also forwards to Config: LegacyConfig() returns a Config instance.

Returned instances

Here, attrs_mapping applies only to class-level attribute access on the proxy. It does not apply to the returned instance.

docs.title: Dataclass field renames
docs.text:
For dataclasses, deprecated_class(attrs_mapping=...) automatically covers two surfaces. Accessing mapped class attributes through the proxy and passing constructor kwargs (DC(old_field=5)) can emit FutureWarning using separate budgets for attribute access and each old constructor keyword. A call with a canonical keyword uses the call-level budget. Returned instances are not wrapped, so their attribute reads are not remapped.

The auto-expansion copies entries targeting dataclass fields from attrs_mapping into args_mapping. Pure field renames therefore need no separate args_mapping.

Auto-expansion never overwrites entries already supplied in an explicit args_mapping.

from dataclasses import dataclass
from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — x and y name the point coordinates
@dataclass
class NewPoint:
    x: float = 0.0
    y: float = 0.0


# DEPRECATED API — px and py redirect to x and y
OldPoint = deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"px": "x", "py": "y"},
    deprecated_in="2.0",
    remove_in="3.0",
    num_warns=-1,
)(NewPoint)

# Constructor kwarg warns: FutureWarning — "px" remapped to "x"
pt = OldPoint(px=1.0)  # warns: FutureWarning
print(pt.x)
Output: pt.x 
1.0

docs.title: Class-type compatibility
docs.text:
Remapping a deprecated kwarg to a POSITIONAL_ONLY constructor parameter emits UserWarning at decoration time. For example, this applies to def __init__(self, val, /): .... At call time, the proxy forwards remapped values positionally through the regular constructor.

This supports required positional-only parameters, frozen or immutable classes, and constructors whose __post_init__ derives state from those values. Run validate_mapping_compatibility(module) in CI to keep these patterns visible.

docs.title: Combining attribute and argument deprecation
docs.text:
The mappings operate on separate surfaces:

Mapping Intercepted surface attrs_mapping Class-level attributes through proxy __getattr__, __setattr__, and __delattr__. args_mapping Call arguments through __call__.

Combine them when a callable target class has renamed class attributes and constructor parameters.

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — lr and epochs configure training
class NewTrainer:
    epochs: int = 10  # class-level default, required for attrs_mapping validation
    lr: float = 0.01  # class-level default, required for attrs_mapping validation

    def __init__(self, lr: float = 0.01, epochs: int = 10) -> None:
        self.lr = lr
        self.epochs = epochs


# DEPRECATED API — learning_rate and n_epochs redirect to the new names
@deprecated_class(
    target=NewTrainer,
    attrs_mapping={"n_epochs": "epochs"},  # class-level attribute rename
    args_mapping={"learning_rate": "lr"},  # constructor argument rename
    deprecated_in="2.0",
    remove_in="3.0",
    num_warns=-1,
)
class LegacyTrainer:
    pass


# The replacement call warns and remaps the keyword to lr.
trainer = LegacyTrainer(learning_rate=0.05)  # warns: FutureWarning
print(trainer.lr)  # NewTrainer instance has lr=0.05

# Warning path 2 — attrs_mapping fires: class-level "n_epochs" redirects to "epochs"
default_epochs = LegacyTrainer.n_epochs  # warns: FutureWarning
print(default_epochs)  # value from NewTrainer.epochs
Output: trainer.lr; default_epochs 
0.05
10

Each deprecated class attribute has its own warning budget. Calls forwarding to a replacement share a call-level budget, even when they use different deprecated keywords. With the default num_warns=1, the proxy emits one warning for calls and one for each deprecated attribute.

docs.title: Mixed redirect and warn-only entries
docs.text:
attrs_mapping accepts string redirects and None for warnings without renaming. Both can coexist alongside args_mapping. One proxy then records every deprecated surface on the class.

The example below deprecates a Model class that renamed its gpu attribute to device and retired the cuda flag entirely. The constructor kwarg n_layers was also renamed to num_layers:

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — device and num_layers configure the model
class Model:
    device: str = "cpu"
    num_layers: int = 4

    def __init__(self, num_layers: int = 4, device: str = "cpu") -> None:
        self.num_layers = num_layers
        self.device = device


# DEPRECATED API — gpu and n_layers redirect; cuda warns without a replacement
@deprecated_class(
    target=Model,
    attrs_mapping={
        "cuda": None,  # warn-only — flag is being removed, still served from LegacyModel
        "gpu": "device",  # redirect — old name "gpu" resolves to Model.device
    },
    args_mapping={"n_layers": "num_layers"},  # constructor kwarg rename
    deprecated_in="3.0",
    remove_in="4.0",
    num_warns=-1,
)
class LegacyModel:
    cuda: bool = False  # being-removed attribute; must live on LegacyModel for warn-only validation


# 1. Constructor — args_mapping fires: "n_layers" remapped to "num_layers"
m = LegacyModel(n_layers=8)  # warns: FutureWarning
print(m.num_layers)

# 2. Attribute redirect — attrs_mapping "gpu" -> "device" fires
print(LegacyModel.gpu)  # warns: FutureWarning

# 3. Warn-only — "cuda" warns but is still served from LegacyModel.cuda
print(LegacyModel.cuda)  # warns: FutureWarning
Output: m.num_layers; LegacyModel.gpu; LegacyModel.cuda 
8
cpu
False

"cuda": None emits FutureWarning on every access in this example. It serves LegacyModel.cuda because Model does not define cuda. "gpu": "device" warns and redirects to Model.device.

At decoration time, every None-value key must exist on at least one class. Define cuda on LegacyModel, or on Model if retaining it in the new API.

Mapping compatibility audit

After combining mappings, run validate_mapping_compatibility(module) from the audit module in CI. It surfaces deprecated kwargs remapped to POSITIONAL_ONLY constructor parameters.

The proxy forwards remapped values positionally. Findings are advisory visibility signals, not failures. Results are DeprecationWrapperInfo objects with non-empty args_mapping_positional_only fields.

See Mapping compatibility for the full pattern.

docs.title: Stacking deprecated_class() for multi-version deprecations
docs.text:
Use one deprecated_class() call when all attributes and arguments share a deprecated_in/remove_in pair. This simplest form keeps both mappings together.

Stack two @deprecated_class() decorators when attributes deprecated in different releases need separate version pairs. For example, steps renamed in v0.8 and lr renamed in v1.0 each need their own removal deadline.

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — learning_rate and max_steps are the canonical configuration names
# DEPRECATED API — each old name keeps its own version pair
# outer layer: v1.0 rename (lr → learning_rate, remove in v2.0)
@deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"lr": "learning_rate"},
    deprecated_in="1.0",
    remove_in="2.0",
)
# inner layer: v0.8 rename (steps → max_steps, remove in v1.0)
@deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"steps": "max_steps"},
    deprecated_in="0.8",
    remove_in="1.0",
)
class LegacyConfig:
    lr: float = 1e-3  # deprecated since 1.0
    learning_rate: float = 1e-3  # canonical
    steps: int = 1000  # deprecated since 0.8
    max_steps: int = 1000  # canonical


cfg = LegacyConfig()
print(LegacyConfig.lr)  # warns: FutureWarning (deprecated in 1.0, remove in 2.0)
print(LegacyConfig.steps)  # warns: FutureWarning (deprecated in 0.8, remove in 1.0)
print(isinstance(cfg, LegacyConfig))
Output: LegacyConfig.lr; LegacyConfig.steps; isinstance(cfg, LegacyConfig) 
0.001
1000
True

Each proxy layer carries its own deprecated_in/remove_in pair. LegacyConfig.lr uses the v1.0 deprecation, while LegacyConfig.steps uses the earlier v0.8 deprecation. Instance reads are not intercepted.

Stacking supports isinstance() and issubclass() through the proxy chain. Instantiation fires at most one global warning.

ATTRS_REMAP layers never warn on instantiation. Two stacked layers warn only on attribute access, using each layer's version pair for its keys.

docs.title: Chained redirect
docs.text:
attrs_mapping accepts multi-hop rename chains such as {"num_iters": "num_steps", "num_steps": "max_steps"}:

  • proxy.num_iters warns once for num_iters and reads the active class's num_steps value directly.
  • proxy.num_steps warns once for num_steps and resolves to max_steps.
  • Audit reports the mapping structure as ChainType.STACKED.

Cycles such as {"a": "b", "b": "a"} raise ValueError at decoration time. Every non-None redirect target in a chain must be a static class attribute. Below, num_steps must exist on the class because num_iters redirects to it:

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — max_steps is the canonical training limit
class TrainLoop:
    max_steps: int = 200
    num_steps: int = max_steps  # redirect target — must exist as a static class attribute


# DEPRECATED API — earlier iteration names resolve through one lookup hop
proxy = deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"num_iters": "num_steps", "num_steps": "max_steps"},
    deprecated_in="2.0",
    remove_in="3.0",
    num_warns=-1,
)(TrainLoop)


val1 = proxy.num_iters  # warns: FutureWarning — num_iters deprecated in v2.0 (→ num_steps)
print(val1)

val2 = proxy.num_steps  # warns: FutureWarning — num_steps deprecated in v2.0 (→ max_steps)
print(val2)

val3 = proxy.max_steps  # silent — canonical name
print(val3)
Output: val1; val2; val3 
200
200
200

Each deprecated name in the chain fires exactly one warning per access (not two). The resolution is a single lookup hop: proxy.num_iters warns for num_iters and then reads TrainLoop.num_steps directly, which at the class level holds the same value as max_steps.

docs.title: Nested proxy wrappers
docs.text:
A deprecated_class proxy can wrap another deprecated_class proxy. The inner proxy handles selective attribute deprecation; the outer proxy adds a blanket class-level deprecation warning on every access regardless of attribute name. The two warning budgets are independent.

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — the canonical colour attribute
class Palette:
    colour: str = "red"
    color: str = colour  # deprecated alias kept for backwards compatibility


# DEPRECATED API — the inner proxy redirects color; the outer proxy deprecates the class
# Inner proxy: warns only when the deprecated alias "color" is accessed
selective_proxy = deprecated_class(
    attrs_mapping={"color": "colour"},
    deprecated_in="1.0",
    remove_in="2.0",
    num_warns=-1,
)(Palette)

# Outer proxy: warns on every attribute access regardless of name
blanket_proxy = deprecated_class(
    deprecated_in="1.0",
    remove_in="2.0",
    num_warns=-1,
)(selective_proxy)


# Accessing the deprecated alias through the outer proxy: two warnings fire —
# first from the inner selective proxy ("color" is deprecated in favor of "colour"),
# then from the outer blanket proxy ("Palette" is deprecated).
print(blanket_proxy.color)  # warns: FutureWarning × 2 — inner selective, then outer blanket

# Accessing the canonical name through the outer proxy: one warning fires —
# only the outer blanket proxy warns; the inner proxy forwards silently.
print(blanket_proxy.colour)  # warns: FutureWarning × 1 — outer blanket only
Output: blanket_proxy.color; blanket_proxy.colour 
red
red

The inner proxy handles the attribute redirect first; the outer proxy then issues its blanket class-deprecation warning. Two warnings fire for blanket_proxy.color — one per proxy layer, the inner color warning before the outer one. Accessing blanket_proxy.colour fires only the outer proxy warning because colour is not listed in the inner proxy's attrs_mapping.

docs.title: Real-world migration: ML training config
docs.text:
This end-to-end example migrates a TrainingConfig dataclass with fields renamed across versions. Existing attribute names keep working while warnings guide users toward the canonical API.

The migration makes these changes:

Surface Change v2.0 → v3.0 attributes lr becomes learning_rate, and n_epochs becomes max_epochs. v3.0 removal size is removed without a replacement, using a warn-only None redirect. Constructor hidden_dim becomes hidden_size. 
from dataclasses import dataclass
from deprecate import deprecated_class, find_deprecation_wrappers


# NEW API — descriptive training configuration names
@dataclass
class TrainingConfig:
    learning_rate: float = 0.001
    max_epochs: int = 100
    hidden_size: int = 256


# DEPRECATED API — old training names redirect or warn until removal
@deprecated_class(
    target=TrainingConfig,
    attrs_mapping={
        "lr": "learning_rate",  # v2.0 rename
        "n_epochs": "max_epochs",  # v2.0 rename
        "size": None,  # removed in v3.0 — warn-only, no replacement
    },
    args_mapping={"hidden_dim": "hidden_size"},  # constructor rename
    deprecated_in="2.0",
    remove_in="3.0",
)
class LegacyTrainingConfig:
    lr: float = 0.001
    learning_rate: float = 0.001
    n_epochs: int = 100
    max_epochs: int = 100
    size: int = 128  # removed in v3.0
    hidden_size: int = 256


# Old attribute names still work — each emits one FutureWarning
print(LegacyTrainingConfig.lr)  # warns: FutureWarning — "lr" → "learning_rate"
print(LegacyTrainingConfig.n_epochs)  # warns: FutureWarning — "n_epochs" → "max_epochs"
print(LegacyTrainingConfig.size)  # warns: FutureWarning — "size" removed (no replacement)
Output: LegacyTrainingConfig.lr; LegacyTrainingConfig.n_epochs; LegacyTrainingConfig.size 
0.001
100
128

# phmdoctest:skip
# Old constructor argument still works — emits one FutureWarning
cfg = LegacyTrainingConfig(hidden_dim=512)  # warns: FutureWarning
print(cfg.hidden_size)
Output: cfg.hidden_size 
512

# phmdoctest:skip
# Audit tools discover the proxy — useful for CI expiry checks
import sys
import types

mod = types.ModuleType("my_ml_lib")
mod.LegacyTrainingConfig = LegacyTrainingConfig
sys.modules["my_ml_lib"] = mod

results = find_deprecation_wrappers(mod)
print(results[0].function, results[0].deprecated_info.deprecated_in)
Output: results[0].function; results[0].deprecated_info.deprecated_in 
LegacyTrainingConfig 2.0

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
See Attributes for selective attribute deprecation and multi-version attribute migrations.

This page covers classes, Enums, dataclasses, and module-level constants. Patterns include forwarding old class names, transparent proxy wrappers, and stacked deprecation layers. For function deprecation, see Functions.

With deprecated_class(update_docstring=True), existing class documentation receives the deprecation notice. A class with __doc__ = None keeps None, without inheriting internal proxy documentation. The original class docstring is unchanged.

docs.title: @deprecated on a class
docs.text:
@deprecated accepts classes directly and dispatches to deprecated_class(), producing an identical _DeprecatedProxy. Everything documented on this page applies to either form, with one exception: the front door forwards only a class target, so a function, functools.partial or callable-instance target on a class source is ignored. Use deprecated_class(target=...) for those.

Class dispatch notice

Dispatch is permanent and is not deprecated. It adds a one-time informational UserWarning, suppressed by stream=None. Only the notice is removed in v1.0.

See Troubleshooting for per-class keying and suppression options. The thread-safe notice cache retains at most 4096 class keys in insertion order. An evicted class may receive the notice again.

from deprecate import deprecated


# NEW/FUTURE API — the replacement class callers should migrate to
class HttpService:
    def call(self) -> str:
        return "ok"


# DEPRECATED API — @deprecated on a class source dispatches to @deprecated_class
@deprecated(target=HttpService, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0")  # warns: UserWarning (one-time dispatch notice)
class LegacyService:
    pass


svc = LegacyService()  # warns: FutureWarning
print(svc.call())
Output: svc.call() 
ok

Prefer @deprecated_class() directly for classes, Enums, and dataclasses. It produces the same result without a dispatch notice and exposes proxy-only options such as attrs_mapping. The rest of this page uses that explicit form.

docs.title: Class deprecation
docs.text:
Choose one of three common patterns:

  • Rename a method with @deprecated(target=execute) on the old name; calls forward to the replacement.
  • Decorate __init__ to warn at instantiation, optionally forwarding construction to a successor class.
  • Rename or retire only some attributes of a class that stays: @deprecated_class(attrs_mapping={"old": "new"}, ...) warns on the listed names and redirects them; see Attributes.

Rename a method within a class:

from deprecate import deprecated, void


class MyService:
    # NEW/FUTURE API — renamed from run() for clarity
    def execute(self, x: int) -> int:
        """Current method."""
        return x * 2

    # DEPRECATED API — `run` was the original name before the rename
    @deprecated(target=execute, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0")
    def run(self, x: int) -> int:
        """Deprecated — renamed to execute()."""
        return void(x)


svc = MyService()
# calling this method will raise a deprecation warning:
#   The `run` was deprecated since v1.0 in favor of `your_module.execute`.
#   It will be removed in v2.0.
print(svc.run(5))
Output: svc.run(5) 
10

Forward __init__ to a successor class. The deprecated class inherits from its successor, preserving all methods and properties on instances:

# NEW/FUTURE API — renamed to be more descriptive
class HttpClient:
    """My new class anywhere in the codebase or other package."""

    def __init__(self, c: float, d: str = "abc"):
        self.my_c = c
        self.my_d = d


# ---------------------------

from deprecate import deprecated, void


# DEPRECATED API — `Client` was the original name before it was renamed to HttpClient
class Client(HttpClient):
    """
    The deprecated class should be inherited from the successor class
     to hold all methods and properties.
    """

    @deprecated(target=HttpClient, deprecated_in="0.2", remove_in="0.4")
    def __init__(self, c: int, d: str = "efg"):
        """
        You place the decorator around __init__ as you want
         to warn user just at the time of creating object.

        Decorating __init__ warns at instantiation time and optionally
        forwards to another class. For deprecating the class itself
        (name change, Enum, dataclass), use @deprecated_class() instead.
        """
        void(c, d)


# calling this function will raise a deprecation warning:
#   The `Client` was deprecated since v0.2 in favor of `your_module.HttpClient`.
#   It will be removed in v0.4.
inst = Client(7)
print(inst.my_c)  # returns: 7
print(inst.my_d)  # returns: "efg"
Output: inst.my_d 
7
efg

docs.title: Constants and instances
docs.text:
deprecated_instance wraps module-level dicts, lists, and custom objects in a transparent proxy. Attribute, item, and call access emit a deprecation notice. Use read_only=True to block attribute and item writes, in-place operators and sixteen standard collection mutators (append, extend, insert, pop, remove, clear, update, setdefault, add, discard, sort, reverse, popitem and the set difference_update, intersection_update, symmetric_difference_update) through the deprecated alias. The guard matches method names on custom objects too. Other methods and nested writes can still mutate the object. See Limitations for the detail.

The proxy carries only protocols supported by the wrapped object:

  • A deprecated settings dict is neither callable(), an Iterator, nor os.PathLike.
  • A deprecated file handle retains context-manager support and iteration.
  • A deprecated Enum class retains len() and iteration.

Arithmetic, unary, and conversion operators forward to the wrapped object. Data-use operations emit deprecation warnings; ordering comparisons, format(), and context exit remain silent structural probes.

When operations consume warnings

Synchronous operations warn only after success. A subscript miss (KeyError) or another failed operation emits nothing and preserves the num_warns budget.

next() warns before advancing the wrapped iterator. An exhausted next() (StopIteration) still warns and spends the budget. A warning raised as an error consumes no item.

__await__ and __anext__ warn when obtaining the underlying awaitable, before it runs. Later rejection or async exhaustion still consumes the warning budget. Calls also warn before execution, like @deprecated.

Fatal operations. With as_exception=True, these operations raise DeprecatedError before touching the wrapped object:

  • Subscripts, iteration, next(), context entry, async iteration, and await raise first.
  • Unary and conversion operators, round(), and in-place operators raise first.

A missing key therefore raises DeprecatedError rather than KeyError, and a defaultdict gains no entry. Binary operators compute first and raise after a successful result.

In-place operators (+=, -=, etc.) return the active object's result rather than a re-wrapped proxy.

Right-hand operands. Python cannot fall back to the proxy when the left-operand type raises TypeError directly, as with "prefix" + proxy_str for str. Put the proxy on the left or wrap the value in a container. See Troubleshooting for details.

A warning filter or custom stream can raise after synchronous or asynchronous context entry acquires a resource. The proxy invokes that context's exit method before propagating the error. Failed underlying entry does not invoke exit.

isinstance(DEFAULTS, dict) returns True: the proxy reports the wrapped object's type through __class__.

Introspection limits

type(DEFAULTS) still returns the wrapper class. Only isinstance, which honours __class__, is transparent; strict type() equality still sees the wrapper.

Detect proxies with isinstance(DEFAULTS, DeprecationProxy) after from deprecate import DeprecationProxy. Never use type(DEFAULTS) is _DeprecatedProxy, which names a private class.

isinstance checks, dunder reads, and failed hasattr probes stay silent. They do not consume the num_warns budget.

Writes never warn. Item writes and deletes (DEFAULTS["lr"] = 0.01, del DEFAULTS["lr"]) follow the attribute-write rule. With read_only=True, writes raise AttributeError unless skip_if evaluates True. During a skip, every write goes directly to the wrapped object.

A deprecated_instance over a plain function can act as a method in a class body: class Model: scale = deprecated_instance(legacy_scale, ...).

  • Through an instance, the proxy binds like the wrapped function. Model().scale(2) calls legacy_scale(model, 2) and warns against one num_warns budget shared across instances.
  • Model().scale is a bound method whose __func__ is the proxy. Consequently, inspect.signature drops self.
  • Through the class, Model.scale is the proxy itself, so Model.scale(model, 2) also works. Use staticmethod(...) around the proxy to keep the function unbound.
  • Proxies over data, classes, and non-function descriptors (property, classmethod, and staticmethod objects) remain as stored and never bind.
  • Only proxies over functions or @deprecated wrappers are descriptors. inspect.isroutine(proxy) is True for these and False for data and class proxies.

Deprecated proxies survive copy.copy() and copy.deepcopy() round-trips. Copies retain the warning behavior and receive independent counters snapshotted from the original.

A shallow proxy copy also tries to copy its replacement data object. After success, top-level writes such as copy["key"] = value do not affect the original replacement. If copying raises, the copy retains the shared replacement, so writes can reach it. Nested mutable values remain shared after a shallow copy. copy.deepcopy can provide independence when the objects support it.

Plain-object deprecated_instance proxies, including dicts, lists, and custom objects, are fully picklable.

Pickling class aliases

A deprecated_class alias raises PicklingError in the common pattern where the proxy replaces the decorated class name. Pickle cannot find the original class by reference. Use copy.deepcopy for class alias proxies instead.

Instances of classes deprecated in place pickle and load as original-class instances without warnings, including exception and OrderedDict subclasses. Classes defining their own __reduce_ex__, such as Enums, are exceptions.

from deprecate import deprecated_instance

# NEW/FUTURE API — renamed to be more explicit about its scope
TRAINING_CONFIG = {"lr": 0.001, "batch_size": 32, "epochs": 10}

# What it looked like before the rename:
# DEFAULTS = {"lr": 0.001, "batch_size": 32, "epochs": 10}

# DEPRECATED API — `DEFAULTS` was the original name; read-only so
# callers cannot mutate shared state through the deprecated alias
DEFAULTS = deprecated_instance(
    TRAINING_CONFIG,
    deprecated_in="1.2",
    remove_in="2.0",
    read_only=True,
)

# Reading still works but emits a FutureWarning once:
#   The `dict` was deprecated since v1.2. It will be removed in v2.0.
print(DEFAULTS["lr"])  # 0.001
Output: DEFAULTS["lr"] 
0.001

docs.title: Serving a replacement object
docs.text:
Pass the replacement as target= (since v0.16) when the old name should already return new values. Attribute, item, operator, and call access use the replacement. The old name keeps warning until removal.

When skip_if evaluates true, operations use the wrapped source without warning or forwarding. Use name= so warnings name the alias callers use.

Built-in warnings name callable replacements only. For a dict or settings object, provide a message_template naming the replacement. See Customization. In generic warnings, %(target_name)s and %(target_path)s render empty for data replacements. Mapped-attribute warnings do fill them.

from deprecate import deprecated_instance

# NEW/FUTURE API — the retry settings that replaced `RETRY_DEFAULTS`
RETRY_POLICY = {"timeout": 30, "retries": 5}

# DEPRECATED API — the old name now serves the new settings and still warns
RETRY_DEFAULTS = deprecated_instance(
    {"timeout": 10, "retries": 3},
    name="RETRY_DEFAULTS",
    target=RETRY_POLICY,
    deprecated_in="1.3",
    remove_in="2.0",
    message_template="`%(source_name)s` is deprecated since v%(deprecated_in)s; use `RETRY_POLICY` instead.",
)

print(RETRY_DEFAULTS["timeout"])  # warns: FutureWarning
Output: RETRY_DEFAULTS["timeout"] 
30

Operations through the old name follow the replacement. isinstance and hashing use it, and writes land on it.

Replacement type compatibility

Proxy protocols combine those of the source and replacement, because skip_if can serve the source. A function replaced by a dict still reports callable(proxy) as True, although calling it raises TypeError.

Keep the replacement's type unchanged or use a subclass unless the type change is intended. A tuple constant replaced by a list becomes unhashable immediately when the deprecation ships.

target=True, target=False, TargetMode.AUTO, and modules raise TypeError. Redirect modules with deprecated_module.

attrs_mapping (since v0.16 on deprecated_instance) deprecates only the listed attribute spellings of an object, the same way it does on a class proxy. Every other attribute stays silent. The mapping covers attributes, not the keys of a mapping object:

from deprecate import deprecated_instance


# NEW/FUTURE API — the display settings spell the attribute `colour`
class DisplaySettings:
    colour = "teal"


# DEPRECATED API — the `color` spelling still works but warns
THEME = deprecated_instance(
    DisplaySettings(), name="THEME", attrs_mapping={"color": "colour"}, deprecated_in="1.3", remove_in="2.0"
)

print(THEME.color)  # warns: FutureWarning
print(THEME.colour)
Output: THEME.color, THEME.colour 
teal
teal

On callable objects, args_mapping (since v0.16 on deprecated_instance) renames keyword arguments. Values renamed onto positional-only parameters are passed positionally.

  • Without target, calls warn only when an old name is used.
  • With a callable target, every call warns because calling the old name is itself deprecated.

Unused call options. On objects that are never called, args_mapping and args_extra cannot apply. They emit UserWarning, becoming TypeError in v1.0.

docs.title: Enums and dataclasses
docs.text:
deprecated_class() wraps an Enum or dataclass in a transparent proxy. It emits deprecation notices and forwards attribute, item, and call operations to the replacement.

  • Use args_mapping to rename or drop kwargs when calling the deprecated class.
  • Without an explicit target, supplying args_mapping auto-resolves to TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP. Warnings occur only when an old argument name is used, matching @deprecated(target=TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP, args_mapping=...).
  • For a no-target ARGS_REMAP proxy, calls using new argument names are silent. A callable replacement target still emits the class-level warning. Structural checks with isinstance and issubclass remain silent.
  • Use args_extra to inject fixed kwargs into every forwarded call. Use message_template to override the warning; both options behave as their @deprecated counterparts do.
  • An Enum rename alias that passes the replacement as its own target (Color = deprecated_class(target=ThemeColor, ...)(ThemeColor)) warns at runtime, and pydeprecate check accepts it. Only a proxy bound back to the class's own name (ThemeColor = deprecated_class(target=ThemeColor, ...)(ThemeColor)) is reported as a no-effect self-reference.
from enum import Enum
from dataclasses import dataclass
from deprecate import deprecated_class

# mypackage/theme.py — what it looked like before the rename:
#
# class Color(Enum):
#     RED = 1
#     BLUE = 2


# NEW/FUTURE API — renamed to be more descriptive
class ThemeColor(Enum):
    RED = 1
    BLUE = 2


# DEPRECATED API — `Color` was the original name; no class body needed,
# the proxy forwards all access to ThemeColor
Color = deprecated_class(target=ThemeColor, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0")(ThemeColor)

# All access is forwarded to ThemeColor — a FutureWarning is emitted once:
#   The `ThemeColor` was deprecated since v1.0 in favor of `<module>.ThemeColor`. It will be removed in v2.0.
print(Color.RED is ThemeColor.RED)  # True
print(Color(1) is ThemeColor.RED)  # True
print(Color["RED"] is ThemeColor.RED)  # True


# Precision migration story:
# - PointV1 used integer pixel coordinates.
# - PointV2 supports float coordinates for sub-pixel precision and smoother transforms.


# NEW/FUTURE API — extended to float precision
@dataclass
class PointV2:
    x: float
    y: float


# DEPRECATED API — PointV1 was the original integer-coordinate implementation
@deprecated_class(target=PointV2, deprecated_in="1.8", remove_in="2.0")
@dataclass
class PointV1:
    x: int
    y: int


# Existing callers using integer coordinates still work and are forwarded to PointV2:
p_old = PointV1(3, 4)
print(isinstance(p_old, PointV2))
print((p_old.x, p_old.y))

# New callers can use higher precision directly:
p_new = PointV2(3.25, 4.75)
print((p_new.x, p_new.y))
Output: (p_new.x, p_new.y) 
True
True
True
True
(3, 4)
(3.25, 4.75)

docs.title: Conditional skip
docs.text:
deprecated_class() and deprecated_instance() accept skip_if: a bool or zero-argument callable returning bool, evaluated at access time.

While the condition evaluates True, the proxy serves the wrapped source unchanged:

  • Warnings and attrs_mapping redirects are disabled.
  • args_mapping, args_extra, target forwarding, and read_only enforcement are disabled.
  • isinstance(proxy, ...), class statements subclassing the alias, and arithmetic operands follow the wrapped source.

Audits never evaluate the condition. Conditions needing a running application therefore do not break find_deprecation_wrappers or the CLI. Callable decorators behave similarly: skipped calls execute the source body unchanged.

Safe skip conditions

A proxy operation may consult the condition more than once. Keep the callable cheap and stable; non-bool results raise TypeError at access time.

Return rather than raise when context is missing. Tools such as help() and pytest --doctest-modules run isinstance on module members, evaluating every proxy's condition.

from deprecate import deprecated_class

MIGRATION_ROLLOUT_DONE = False


def rollout_pending() -> bool:
    return not MIGRATION_ROLLOUT_DONE


# NEW/FUTURE API — the replacement backend callers should migrate to
class StorageBackend:
    def save(self) -> str:
        return "stored"


# DEPRECATED API — deprecation stays dormant until the rollout flag flips
@deprecated_class(target=StorageBackend, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0", skip_if=rollout_pending)
class LegacyStorage:
    def save(self) -> str:
        return "legacy-stored"


store = LegacyStorage()  # silent — skip active, source class served, no target forwarding
print(store.save())
Output: store.save() 
legacy-stored

Once the condition flips to False, the very next access warns and forwards to the target as usual — no re-decoration required.

docs.title: Type annotations and static analysis
docs.text:
At runtime, deprecated_class() returns a proxy. Type checkers model the class it forwards to.

The call form deprecated_class(target=BrandColor, ...)(WidgetColor) has type type[BrandColor] regardless of the wrapped class. The alias therefore checks against the replacement.

With the decorator form, mypy ignores a class decorator's return type, leaving the name typed as the decorated class. Pyright applies it, so @deprecated_class(target=BrandColor, ...) produces type[BrandColor]:

from enum import Enum
from deprecate import DeprecationProxy, deprecated_class


# NEW/FUTURE API — renamed to describe the palette rather than the widget
class BrandColor(Enum):
    RED = 1
    BLUE = 2


# DEPRECATED API — `WidgetColor` was the original name; `target=BrandColor` types the alias as `type[BrandColor]`
WidgetColor = deprecated_class(target=BrandColor, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0")(BrandColor)

print(WidgetColor(1) is BrandColor.RED)  # warns: FutureWarning
print(isinstance(BrandColor.BLUE, WidgetColor))
print(isinstance(WidgetColor, DeprecationProxy))
Output: WidgetColor(1) is BrandColor.RED; isinstance(BrandColor.BLUE, WidgetColor); isinstance(WidgetColor, DeprecationProxy) 
True
True
True

Type-checking behavior depends on how the alias is used:

  • Class checks succeed. isinstance(x, WidgetColor) and issubclass(...) narrow to BrandColor. WidgetColor(1), member and attribute access, and passing the alias as type[BrandColor] also type-check. Each forwards to the class at runtime.
  • The alias is a variable, not a type. Every checker rejects def paint(color: WidgetColor), and mypy also rejects class Child(WidgetColor). Annotate with the replacement class, or use the decorator form in mypy to retain a class statement.
  • Missing old names are flagged. Renamed kwargs and attributes absent from the wrapped class trigger call-arg and attr-defined errors, as in the decorator form. Retain old names in a legacy class body to keep calls type-checking during migration.
  • An explicit proxy cast permits old names. Use cast(DeprecationProxy[Config], deprecated_class(...)(Config)) for permissive calls and attributes. The trade-off is that isinstance against this alias no longer type-checks.
  • A class target determines the type. With target=BrandColor, the alias is type[BrandColor] even when wrapping a separate legacy class. WidgetColor(...) has the BrandColor instance type returned at runtime.
  • Without a class target, the wrapped type remains. This includes args_mapping-only and attrs_mapping-only wrappers. With skip_if, the type models the steady state; keep the wrapped class compatible with target while serving it during skips.
  • The @deprecated front door cannot see target statically. A class decorated with @deprecated(target=BrandColor, ...) keeps its wrapped-class type despite runtime forwarding. Use deprecated_class(target=BrandColor, ...) for type[BrandColor].
  • Proxy-only attributes are invisible on type[BrandColor]. Read __deprecation_config__ with get_deprecation_config(WidgetColor) and unwrap with inspect.unwrap(WidgetColor). Alternatively, use cast(DeprecationProxy[Any], WidgetColor) at the site needing these attributes.

DeprecationProxy[T] remains the annotation for deprecated_instance() proxies, where T is the type calling the proxy produces.

Functional aliases keep the source name. Warnings name the wrapped class, not the assigned variable. The example reports `BrandColor`. Wrap a source class with the name callers know, or provide message_template.

isinstance only. DeprecationProxy declares attributes as well as methods, making it a data protocol. isinstance(obj, DeprecationProxy) works. issubclass(SomeType, DeprecationProxy) raises TypeError, like every runtime-checkable protocol with non-method members.

docs.title: Breadcrumbs for documentation and IDE tools
docs.text:
Every proxy carries two attributes that let static tooling see through it to the original object:

Attribute Points to Used by __wrapped__ the source class or object inspect.unwrap, Sphinx autodoc, griffe/mkdocstrings, IDEs __signature__ the source's signature inspect.signature and anything that does not walk __wrapped__

Reading either attribute has no side effects or deprecation notices. Documentation builds and IDE hovers stay quiet:

import inspect
from dataclasses import dataclass
from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW/FUTURE API — renamed for clarity
@dataclass
class RetryPolicy:
    attempts: int
    backoff: float = 1.0


# DEPRECATED API — `RetryConfig` was the original name
@deprecated_class(target=RetryPolicy, deprecated_in="1.4", remove_in="2.0")
@dataclass
class RetryConfig:
    attempts: int
    backoff: float = 1.0


# No warning — the breadcrumbs are read straight off the proxy
print(inspect.unwrap(RetryConfig).__name__)
print(str(inspect.signature(RetryConfig)))
Output: inspect.unwrap(RetryConfig).__name__; str(inspect.signature(RetryConfig)) 
RetryConfig
(attempts: int, backoff: float = 1.0) -> None

Objects without introspectable signatures receive __signature__ = None, rather than raising. A plain dict wrapped by deprecated_instance() is one example. Failed source introspection never prevents wrapping.

docs.title: PEP 702 static checkers
docs.text:
Stack typing_extensions.deprecated or warnings.deprecated directly above @deprecated_class(...) to flag every old-class use in mypy and pyright. Supply category=None and a string-literal message. See Functions → Static type checkers.

With a class target, the checkers infer different types:

  • Mypy ignores the class decorator's return type, retaining the old class statement. Mirror the replacement's constructor and methods in the old class body for accurate checking.
  • Pyright applies the return type, producing type[ReportWriter] in the example below. It already checks calls against the replacement.

The PEP 702 message lives on the proxy, leaving the replacement class unmarked. It survives copy.copy, copy.deepcopy, and pickle round-trips of the alias.

After del alias.__deprecated__, the attribute reads as missing. It does not fall through to the wrapped class.

import typing_extensions

from deprecate import deprecated_class


# NEW API — the renamed writer
class ReportWriter:
    def __init__(self, path: str = "") -> None:
        self.path = path


# DEPRECATED API — flagged by mypy, forwarded with a warning at runtime
@typing_extensions.deprecated("Use `ReportWriter` instead.", category=None)
@deprecated_class(target=ReportWriter, deprecated_in="1.2", remove_in="2.0")
class CsvReportWriter:
    def __init__(self, path: str = "") -> None:
        self.path = path


print(CsvReportWriter("out.csv").path)  # warns: FutureWarning
print("__deprecated__" in vars(ReportWriter))
Output: CsvReportWriter("out.csv").path; "__deprecated__" in vars(ReportWriter) 
out.csv
False

docs.title: Fatal deprecations
docs.text:
as_exception=True works on deprecated_class() and deprecated_instance() as on callable forms. See Fatal deprecations for the full contract.

Operations that would warn raise DeprecatedError instead:

  • Instantiation, warning-producing attribute reads, item access, and calls become fatal.
  • Data-use arithmetic and conversion dunders become fatal.
  • Writes to names listed in attrs_mapping raise before the mapped write.

Ordinary attribute writes and access outside an active attrs_mapping stay silent. Constructor-only TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP does not make attribute access fatal.

Structural probes remain silent: isinstance, issubclass, repr, str, equality, ordering, and len never warned.

Fatal attribute probes. Without attrs_mapping, a missing attribute makes hasattr return False silently. Successful non-dunder lookups on warning-producing paths raise DeprecatedError, which hasattr does not swallow. With attrs_mapping, listed names raise before lookup even when missing. Unlisted names stay silent whether present or missing.

Fatal deprecation is not an authorization boundary

Without attrs_mapping, attribute lookup resolves the value before reaching the fatal warning path. A property getter or descriptor can therefore produce side effects before DeprecatedError.

If the getter raises its own exception, that exception propagates first. Mapped attribute reads reach the fatal path before resolving the mapped descriptor.

docs.title: Deprecation Messages and Templates
docs.text: pyDeprecate picks a deprecation message template automatically based on how you configured the decorator. Override it with message_template when the defaults do not fit.

docs.title: Default templates
docs.text:
Three built-in templates cover the common scenarios:

Template When it fires Example output TEMPLATE_WARNING_CALLABLE target is a callable (function forwarding) The `score` was deprecated since v1.0 in favor of `pkg.score_predictions`. It will be removed in v2.0. TEMPLATE_WARNING_ARGUMENTS TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP with args_mapping and the caller passes a deprecated argument The `my_func` uses deprecated arguments: `lr` -> `learning_rate`. They were deprecated since v1.0 and will be removed in v2.0. TEMPLATE_WARNING_NO_TARGET TargetMode.NOTIFY (notice-only, no forwarding) The `legacy_func` was deprecated since v1.0. It will be removed in v2.0.

The selection logic is:

  1. If target is a callable (function, method, or class) → TEMPLATE_WARNING_CALLABLE
  2. If TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP and the caller passes a deprecated argument from args_mapping → TEMPLATE_WARNING_ARGUMENTS
  3. If TargetMode.NOTIFY → TEMPLATE_WARNING_NO_TARGET

When you provide message_template, your custom template replaces whichever default would have been chosen.

docs.title: Placeholder variables
docs.text:
Custom templates use Python %-style formatting (%(key)s). Available placeholders depend on the deprecation type:

Placeholder Available when Value source_name Always Name of the deprecated function (e.g. "score") source_path Always Fully qualified path (e.g. "mypackage.score") target_name target is callable Name of the replacement function target_path target is callable Fully qualified path of the replacement deprecated_in Always Value of deprecated_in parameter remove_in Always Value of remove_in parameter argument_map TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP with args_mapping Formatted string like `old` -> `new`

With deprecated_class and deprecated_instance, source_path depends on what the proxy wraps:

  • a class (or a plain function) gives its module-qualified path, e.g. "mypackage.LegacyConfig";
  • an instance has no module of its own, so the path is the proxy's name, e.g. "config_dict";
  • a deprecated attrs_mapping attribute appends the attribute name, e.g. "mypackage.LegacyConfig.old_attr" (its source_name is the attribute name).

The TEMPLATE_WARNING_* constants live in deprecate.messaging (for example from deprecate.messaging import TEMPLATE_WARNING_CALLABLE). An unknown placeholder or a malformed conversion in message_template raises ValueError at decoration time, listing the available placeholders.

An empty deprecated_in emits a UserWarning at decoration time, except when stream=None or a message_template is set; deprecated_module honours only the message_template, because stream=None still delivers its module warning until v1.0.

Proxy warnings pick their template by warning kind, as @deprecated does:

  • a call through deprecated_class or deprecated_instance uses the shared call-level TEMPLATE_WARNING_CALLABLE budget when a replacement target is set, including calls with old args_mapping names. The default num_warns=1 emits one warning per proxy and num_warns=-1 emits one per call.
  • a call with an old keyword in TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP or an automatically expanded dataclass field mapping to the wrapped class uses the keyword's own TEMPLATE_WARNING_ARGUMENTS budget. The new argument name fills target_name.
  • an attrs_mapping access sets source_name to the old attribute and target_name to the new attribute name, and target_path to Owner.attr.

docs.title: Custom template example
docs.text:
from deprecate import TargetMode, deprecated


# NEW API — detects objects and returns a scaled count
def detect_objects(x: int) -> int:
    return x * 10


# DEPRECATED API — `detect` replaced by `detect_objects`
@deprecated(
    target=detect_objects,
    deprecated_in="2.0",
    remove_in="3.0",
    message_template=("[MIGRATION] `%(source_name)s` is removed in v%(remove_in)s. Switch to `%(target_path)s`."),
)
def detect(x: int) -> int:
    pass


# Emits: [MIGRATION] `detect` is removed in v3.0. Switch to `your_module.detect_objects`.
result = detect(5)
print(result)
Output: detect(5) 
50

For argument deprecation, a custom template that references the mapping:

from deprecate import TargetMode, deprecated


@deprecated(
    target=TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP,
    deprecated_in="1.5",
    remove_in="2.0",
    args_mapping={"lr": "learning_rate"},
    message_template="%(source_name)s: renamed args %(argument_map)s (since v%(deprecated_in)s, removal v%(remove_in)s)",
)
def train(lr: float = 0.01, learning_rate: float = 0.01) -> float:
    return learning_rate


# Emits: train: renamed args `lr` -> `learning_rate` (since v1.5, removal v2.0)
print(train(lr=0.001))
Output: train(lr=0.001) 
0.001

docs.title: Deprecation Output Sink (stream)
docs.text:
stream controls where deprecation messages go. It accepts a callable that can receive the warning message, or None to silence output entirely.

pyDeprecate probes the callable signature to see whether it can also receive stacklevel. If that signature cannot be inspected, it calls the stream with the message only. In that fallback, a custom stream that forwards to warnings.warn cannot receive pyDeprecate's caller stack level.

The stream runs exactly once per warning — a TypeError it raises is never retried — so the decision is made from its signature before the call:

Stream signature Call It accepts a stacklevel keyword through a named parameter or **kwargs. It receives stream(msg, stacklevel=...). Any other signature applies. It receives stream(msg).

Forwarding stacklevel

A stream declaring **kwargs is handed stacklevel= and must accept or drop it. Forward it to a callable that takes it (warnings.warn, logging.warning). Never forward it to one that rejects it: print(msg, **kwargs) raises TypeError.

To receive the message alone, declare the stream without **kwargs.

A bare (*args, **kwargs) pass-through built with functools.wraps is judged by the callable it wraps. An adapter around a message-only sink therefore stays message-only. A narrow stream that only copied another callable's metadata is judged by its own parameters.

docs.title: Default: FutureWarning via warnings.warn
docs.text:
By default, stream is functools.partial(warnings.warn, category=FutureWarning). In practice this means:

  • Deprecation notices appear as FutureWarning, visible by default in scripts and interactive sessions.
  • Standard warning filters apply — suppress with warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=FutureWarning) when needed.
  • The warning points at your line that calls the deprecated API, not at pyDeprecate's wrapper code.

The location is measured when the warning fires, skipping every frame inside the deprecate package. Module-scoped warning filters and -W error tracebacks therefore name your code.

A custom stream receives the same stacklevel. A Python stream forwarding it to warnings.warn adds its own frame and lands one frame short. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Silencing deprecation output entirely
docs.text:
Pass stream=None to disable all deprecation output for a specific function. Call forwarding still works — only the message is suppressed. This is useful for internal wrappers that exist solely for backwards compatibility without user-facing noise.

Testing with stream=None

When stream=None is set, no FutureWarning is emitted, so pytest.warns(FutureWarning) will fail. Test the call-forwarding result directly instead of asserting the warning. See Testing Deprecated Code for patterns.

from deprecate import deprecated


def _compute(x: int) -> int:
    return x + 1


@deprecated(target=_compute, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0", stream=None)
def _compute_raw(x: int) -> int:
    pass


# No warning emitted, but call is still forwarded to _compute
print(_compute_raw(5))
Output: _compute_raw(5) 
6

docs.title: Redirecting to a logger
docs.text:
Pass logging.warning (or any logging level method) to route deprecation messages through Python's logging system. This plugs straight into your existing log aggregation, filtering, and formatting.

import logging
from deprecate import deprecated

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)


# NEW API — sorts a list and returns the sorted copy
def sort_items(data: list) -> list:
    return sorted(data)


# DEPRECATED API — `process_batch` replaced by `sort_items`
@deprecated(
    target=sort_items,
    deprecated_in="1.0",
    remove_in="2.0",
    stream=logging.warning,
)
def process_batch(data: list) -> list:
    pass


# Instead of a FutureWarning, this emits a WARNING-level log line:
#   WARNING:root:The `process_batch` was deprecated since v1.0 in favor of `your_module.sort_items`.
#   It will be removed in v2.0.
print(process_batch([3, 1, 2]))
Output: process_batch([3, 1, 2]) 
[1, 2, 3]

Pick the log level that matches the urgency:

  • logging.warning — standard choice; visible in default configs
  • logging.error — critical deprecations nearing removal deadline
  • logging.info — low-priority deprecations during early migration

Combine num_warns=-1 with stream=logging.warning for migration tracking

With unlimited notices routed to your logger, every deprecated call site appears in your log aggregation system (ELK, Datadog, CloudWatch). Query the logs to measure migration progress and find remaining callers before the removal deadline.

docs.title: Using print for simple console output
docs.text:
Use print for quick debugging or scripts where you want immediate stdout output without the warnings module:

from deprecate import deprecated


# NEW API — formats a greeting string for the given name
def say_hello(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}!"


# doc-example only: forces realistic path in warning; real modules set __module__ automatically
say_hello.__module__ = "your_module"


# DEPRECATED API — `greet` replaced by `say_hello`
@deprecated(target=say_hello, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0", stream=print)
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    pass


# Prints directly to stdout:
#   The `greet` was deprecated since v1.0 in favor of `your_module.say_hello`.
#   It will be removed in v2.0.
print(greet("World"))
Output: greet("World") 
The `greet` was deprecated since v1.0 in favor of `your_module.say_hello`. It will be removed in v2.0.
Hello, World!

docs.title: Custom stream callable
docs.text:
Any callable accepting the message as a single string argument works. One that also declares stacklevel or **kwargs is additionally passed stacklevel= and must accept or drop it. See Deprecation Output Sink.

This example collects deprecation messages into a list for later processing:

from deprecate import deprecated

collected_warnings: list = []


def collector(msg: str) -> None:
    collected_warnings.append(msg)


# NEW API — doubles the input value
def target_fn(x: int) -> int:
    return x * 2


# doc-example only: forces realistic path in warning; real modules set __module__ automatically
target_fn.__module__ = "your_module"


# DEPRECATED API — `source_fn` replaced by `target_fn`
@deprecated(target=target_fn, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0", stream=collector)
def source_fn(x: int) -> int:
    pass


source_fn(10)
print(collected_warnings)
Output: print(collected_warnings) 
['The `source_fn` was deprecated since v1.0 in favor of `your_module.target_fn`. It will be removed in v2.0.']
